tropes.html: Mini-Me is ejected out into space unprotected, and survives completely unharmed (though Dr. Evil thinks this warrants a flu shot).

tropes.name: Big Little Man
tropes.html: Mini-Me's introduction. Upon the announcement that Dr. Evil has been cloned, a regular-sized silhouette of him is outside the door. The door open revealing that said clone is tiny.

tropes.name: Bilingual Bonus
tropes.html: "As the French would say, it has a certain... I don't know what." The phrase je ne sais quoi, a popular term borrowed from French to describe some indescribable aspect of something, literally translates to 'I don't know what'.

tropes.name: Blatant Lies
tropes.html: When Basil tells Felicity not to get too close to Austin, she retorts that her interest in this case is "purely professional" - despite the fact that she had just tried to sleep with Austin.

tropes.name: British Royal Guards
tropes.html: Has a montage where Austin and Felicity goad a royal guard into participating in a Motionless Makeover.

tropes.name: Bulletproof Human Shield
tropes.html:
Robin Swallows can protect Austin from machine gun fire and a bazooka rocket.
Austin: Why Won't You Die?!

tropes.name: Call-Back
tropes.html: Scott suggests that Dr. Evil just go back in time and kill Austin "while he's sitting on the crapper", a nod to Paddy O'Brien's assassination attempt on Austin in the first film.

tropes.name: Captain Obvious
tropes.html: Fat Bastard, after cutting one: "Sorry. I farted."

tropes.name: Censored Title
tropes.html: The movie was often advertised in Britain as "The Spy Who...", leaving out the last two words. In Britain, "shag" is a much dirtier word than it is in North America. Averted or inverted (depending on whether the new title is considered more offensive than the original) in Norway, however, where the title translated as The Spy Who Spermed Me.

tropes.name: Cluster F-Bomb
tropes.html: The Jerry Springer scene. All censored, of course.

tropes.name: Convection, Schmonvection
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's hollowed-out volcano lair, in particular the Lava Pit Death Trap that only burns you if you fall in.

tropes.name: Conveniently Empty Roads
tropes.html: Austin and Felicity are chased down the countryside by one of Dr. Evil's assassins. Not only do they not pass a single other car during the chase, but no one drives by after they capture and interrogate the assassin.

tropes.name: *Cough* Snark *Cough*
tropes.html: Scott mocks Dr. Evil saying his laser will turn the moon into what he calls a "death star" by pretending to cough in order to hide him saying "Ripoff!"

tropes.name: Covert Pervert
tropes.html: When Austin's arrival in the past causes a women to faint, a man catches her... and proceeds to gawk at her figure. This same fellow also openly stares at Felicity's chest when she pulls him in for a dance.

tropes.name: Delayed Ripple Effect
tropes.html: While Fat Bastard steals Austin's mojo in 1969, Austin only realizes he's lost it in 1999.

tropes.name: Distaff Counterpart
tropes.html: In many ways, Felicity is the female equivalent to Austin. With Austin in his currently diminished state, meeting someone who is more like him than he is at the moment further afffects his self-confidence (especially when he forces himself to turn down Felicity's offer of sex).

tropes.name: Does This Remind You of Anything?
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's rocket has a long, slender fuselage and two spherical fuel tanks near the thruster.

tropes.name: Establishing Character Music
tropes.html: Felicity makes her presence known to Austin by dancing provocatively to "American Woman" by The Guess Who.

tropes.name: Even Evil Has Standards
tropes.html:
• Played both ways and for levity during The Jerry Springer Show sequence. Even the Neo-Nazi and the Klansman think Dr. Evil's a freak (and the latter calls him out as such). Dr. Evil, for his part, becomes angry at the Klansman’s verbal disparaging of Scott. Their relationship may be strained, but even Dr. Evil’s not going to let anyone talk to his own son that way (and attacks the Klansman in retaliation).
  • Dr. Evil then invokes it again later when Fat Bastard mocks Austin after learning Felicity slept with the Scotsman. As much as Dr. Evil enjoys seeing Austin in any kind of agony, having to also imagine Fat Bastard naked is just too gross.

tropes.name: Eye Scream
tropes.html: Mini-Me jams his thumbs into Austin's eyes during their fight on the moon.

tropes.name: Failed a Spot Check
tropes.html: When the Fembot Vanessa unleashes her "machine gun jubblies", Austin playfully wonders how he could have missed those during their lovemaking. The Fembot coldly responds "Perhaps next time you should try foreplay!"

tropes.name: Fan Disservice
tropes.html: Naked Fat Bastard. Send the Brain Bleach! Dr. Evil even lampshades this in-universe.

tropes.name: Fantastic Plagiarism
tropes.html: While he's in the past, Dr. Evil claims credit for various contemporary pop cultural fads, such as claiming "One of Us" was a song he invented. Of course, Scott starts calling him out when he comes back.

tropes.name: Faux Paw
tropes.html: When Austin first sees Felicity, He licks his hand and grooms himself like a cat, in some kind of enticement ritual. He follows up by pushing his "paws" forward as he makes his way toward Felicity.

tropes.name: Flirting Under Fire
tropes.html: Austin and Felicity have a tender moment... while standing in a laughably pathetic Death Trap.

tropes.name: Forced Dance Partner
tropes.html:
Austin is drawn to the beautiful and flirty Felicity Shagwell. Before he can embrace her, Robin Swallows suddenly pops up inbetween them, pushing Austin across the dance floor and away from Felicity, to Austin's distress.
Austin: (reaches for Felicity) I want! I want!!

tropes.name: Foreshadowing
tropes.html: Immediately after Frau tells Dr. Evil that she's late, Scott comes through the time portal and joins them. In The Stinger, we learn that he's not a test tube baby, but Dr. Evil and Frau's love child.

tropes.name: A Glass in the Hand
tropes.html: Vanessa in the beginning smashes a champagne bottle in her hand.

tropes.name: GPS Evidence
tropes.html: The heroes are able to find the location of Dr. Evil's volcano lair by analyzing Fat Bastard's stool sample, discovering traces of a rare vegetable that only grows on one island in the entire world.

tropes.name: Hand Signals
tropes.html: Felicity Shagwell uses them to tell her agents to interfere with Robin Spitz Swallows.

tropes.name: Hand Wave
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's new volcano lair is stated to have been built after past Number Two received a "memo from the future".

tropes.name: Happy Ending Override
tropes.html: The film opens on Austin and Vanessa's honeymoon, whereupon Vanessa reveals herself as a Fembot and self destructs.

tropes.name: Head-Turning Beauty
tropes.html: Felicity catches Austin's eye from across the room, and quickly gains the attention of a couple of other men on her way over to him.

tropes.name: Held Gaze
tropes.html: In her first scene, Felicity locks eyes with Austin from across the room, and keeps looking at him even as she dances with two other guys.

tropes.name: Heroic Seductress
tropes.html: Felicity charms Fat Bastard into bed with her so she can plant a tracking device on him.

tropes.name: High-Heel–Face Turn
tropes.html: Ivana Humpalot was sent to kill Austin, but she ends up confessing and sleeping with him instead, simply unable to resist him.

tropes.name: Hoist Hero over Head
tropes.html: Mini-Me lifts Austin up easily (in spite of his small stature), spins him around, then throws him across the corridor.

tropes.name: Hypocritical Humor
tropes.html: After Austin escapes two assassination attempts in a row, Dr. Evil voices his disappointment, claiming that he is "the man who will maintain the dignity of this evil organization"... while driving around in a scooter (with Mini-Me repeatedly honking the horn).

tropes.name: I Ate WHAT?!
tropes.html:
Austin drinks Fat Bastard's stool sample, thinking it is coffee.
Austin: This coffee smells like shit.
Basil: It is shit, Austin.
Austin: Oh, good, then it's not just me. [drinks more] It's a bit nutty.

tropes.name: I'm Mr. [Future Pop Culture Reference]
tropes.html: Dr. Evil uses footage from the film Independence Day to frighten the president and others into thinking the White House is being attacked. But tells him that's what's gonna happen. He calls his moon laser the Death Star and the task of assembling it The Alan Parsons Project. Having gone back to 1969, however, only Scott realizes the idiocy.

tropes.name: Implacable Man
tropes.html: Played for laughs with assassin Robin Spitz-Swallows: she survives a knife in the back, a dozen bullets in the back, a shot from a bazooka in the face, and a ridiculously high fall out of a window with Austin landing on top of her. A spot of Lampshade Hanging occurs when Austin cries "Why won't you die?!" A deleted scene shows that he keeps her in the trunk of his car to deflect gunfire.

tropes.name: Improbable Aiming Skills
tropes.html: Towards the end, Austin fires fewer shots from his handgun than the number of henchmen he hits.

tropes.name: Inelegant Blubbering
tropes.html: Austin openly weeps after the first phase of Mini-Me's attack.

tropes.name: Inflation Negation
tropes.html: Inverted. Dr. Evil's 1969 ransom of one hundred billion dollars doesn't even exist yet.

tropes.name: Instant Seduction
tropes.html: Upon imbibing some of the stolen mojo, Dr. Evil immediately manages to charm Frau.

tropes.name: Intangible Theft
tropes.html: Fat Bastard steals Austin Powers' "mojo" (his libido and sexual prowess) for his arch-nemesis Dr. Evil. It's visualized as a red liquid with little male symbols floating in it.

tropes.name: Intimate Lotion Application
tropes.html: Felicity asks Austin to give her a Massage of Love, which first involves rubbing her back with scented oils. Since Austin has recently lost his mojo (the part of him that makes him so confident and skilled with women), he approaches the act with awkwardness and nervousness, and when she shows her bare back to him he ends up squeezing the bottle so hard the oil spills out.

tropes.name: Island Base
tropes.html: One of Doctor Evil's Evil Lairs.

tropes.name: I Surrender, Suckers!
tropes.html: During their fight in Dr. Evil's moon base, Mini-Me goves Austin the Peace sign, indicating he doesn't want to fight anymore. Austin accepts, only for Mini-Me to attack him while his guard is down.

tropes.name: It's Personal
tropes.html: Both Dr. Evil and Austin say this this in reference to how Dr. Evil's stolen Austin's mojo.

tropes.name: It Was with You All Along
tropes.html: Austin despairs after his mojo is destroyed, believing he's "useless" without it. Felicity points out that he actually had it with him all along, as he was still able to save the world from Dr. Evil.

tropes.name: Lame Comeback
tropes.html:
When Fat Bastard suggests that he and Felicity could have "another go", Austin retaliates rather feebly:
Austin: Shut your mouth, you bastard! ...Who is fat.

tropes.name: Lava Is Boiling Kool-Aid
tropes.html: Though Convection, Schmonvection is played straight, this trope is surprisingly averted. Objects (and people) which fall into the lava do not sink to the bottom, and at no point does the lava "flow".

tropes.name: Leno Device
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's return is announced to the world via...him and Scott appearing on The Jerry Springer Show.

tropes.name: Literalist Snarking
tropes.html:
• Vanessa asks Austin if he smokes after sex. Austin's response? "I don't know, baby. I never look!"
  • Another example is from Austin and Felicity's first meeting.
    Austin: Those are skintight. How do you get into those pants, baby?
    Felicity: You can start by buying me a drink.

tropes.name: The Loins Sleep Tonight
tropes.html: Austin, while in the middle of sex with Dr. Evil's spy Ivana Humpalot, suddenly loses his erection in 1999 when his mojo (libido/sex drive/virility) is stolen from his cryogenically frozen body in 1969. He then travels back to the Swingin' Sixties to reclaim his mojo and cure his erectile dysfunction. His desire to get his groove back is only heightened when the sexy spy/hippie Felicity Shagwell comes his way. With both wanting to shag each other, Felicity increases the swinger's desire to cure his impotency and get his mojo back from Dr. Evil so Austin and Felicity can finally do the horizontal tango.

tropes.name: Marshmallow Hell
tropes.html:
While scoping out Dr. Evil's headquarters, Austin is accidentally pulled down into Felicity's breasts.
Austin: Hello, mummy. Mummy, can I have some chocolates? I want some Mars bars! Don't smack my bottom, mummy...

tropes.name: MST3K Mantra
tropes.html: Invoked and lampshaded, when Austin has some issues with temporal causality. Basil Exposition tells him to just relax and try to enjoy it, then looks directly at the camera and tells the audience to do the same.

tropes.name: Naked People Are Funny
tropes.html: The opening credits play over a scene wherein Austin decides to celebrate his newfound singleness by taking a stroll through the hotel in the buff, his naughty parts concealed by various objects.

tropes.name: Neck Lift
tropes.html: Vanessa does this with Austin in the opening scene.

tropes.name: Never the Selves Shall Meet
tropes.html:
Averted, when Austin not only interacts with a ten-minute-younger version of himself, but the two of them apparently wind up engaging in a three-way with Felicity Shagwell.
Austin Powers: Technically it's not cheating, baby!

tropes.name: Never Trust a Trailer
tropes.html: An early trailer made it seem like Robin Swallows had a larger role then she actually did.

tropes.name: No-Holds-Barred Beatdown
tropes.html: Mini-Me inflicts a brutal assault upon Austin, enough that Austin at one point tearfully pleads "No more!"

tropes.name: Not Actually the Ultimate Question
tropes.html:
When Austin asks Felicity how she could sleep with Fat Bastard, she tells him she was only doing her job. Austin replies that he meant that literally, as Fat Bastard is so fat that the idea of him even being able to have sex seems physically impossible.
Austin: The man's so fat, the sheer mechanics of it are mind-boggling.

tropes.name: Not So Above It All
tropes.html:
Jerry Springer gets into a fight with Dr Evil on his show.
Dr. Evil: "He's biting me! He's biting me!"

tropes.name: Offscreen Teleportation
tropes.html: When Dr. Evil and Mini-Me board the rocket to the moon, they are saluted by his minions who then somehow appear on the moon when they get there.

tropes.name: Once More, with Volume!
tropes.html:
Austin is giving a massage to Felicity who, upon being asked how it feels, requests Austin to move his hands further down along her back. Austin misinterprets and asks his same question but with a deeper voice.
Austin: [giving Felicity a massage] How does that feel, baby?
Felicity: Mmm, lower!
Austin: [deeper voice] How does that feel, baby?

tropes.name: O.O.C. Is Serious Business
tropes.html: After Felicity dies, Austin chases Dr. Evil down with the intent to kill him. As in, not with the purpose of arresting a dangerous felon as within his duty as an international man of mystery, but hunting down Dr. Evil for the express purpose of murdering him. Dr. Evil only saves himself by mentioning that Austin could undo Felicity's death by using time travel.

tropes.name: Opening Narration
tropes.html: The late Tony Jay provides the narration for the film's Opening Scroll.

tropes.name: Parody Product Placement
tropes.html: Starbucks features quite heavily in the 90s-set portion of the movie... where it's revealed to be owned by Dr. Evil, courtesy of Number Two's prudent investing. Indeed, his new Supervillain Lair is a (fictional) Starbucks atop the Space Needle. Two even tries to persuade Evil to focus his business more on coffee than evil empires, on the grounds that they'll make a lot more money that way, but Evil is having none of it.

tropes.name: Perspective Reversal
tropes.html: In the first film, Austin upsets Vanessa by sleeping with Alotta as part of the job; in this movie, Felicity upsets Austin by sleeping with Fat Bastard as part of the job.

tropes.name: Pop-Cultural Osmosis Failure
tropes.html: Justified via Dr. Evil's frequent usage of references in his ransom video to the president; they were from media which doesn't even exist yet at the time. Funnily enough, this works in his favor when he "demonstrates" the laser's power by playing footage of the White House blowing up ripped straight from Independence Day, which initially scares everyone in the room into thinking that it was real.

tropes.name: Post-Climax Confrontation
tropes.html: Done with Fat Bastard but he gets defeated with a Groin Attack.

tropes.name: Prove I Am Not Bluffing
tropes.html: Dr. Evil blows up the White House to demonstrate his giant moon based laser... except it was just footage from Independence Day. Dr. Evil defends the real laser effect would be very similar.

tropes.name: Pun
tropes.html: Fat Bastard declares "I have more chins than a Chinese phone book!" when lamenting to Austin and Felicity about his weight.

tropes.name: Riddled and Rattled
tropes.html: Robin's body shakes wildly when Austin's uses her as a shield against a machine gun barrage.

tropes.name: Ridiculous Counter-Request
tropes.html:
When Ivana Humpalot says her name and Austin thinks she's making a request, he replies:
"Yeah, and I want a toilet made out of solid gold. It's just not in the cards now, is it?"

tropes.name: Robotic Reveal
tropes.html: When Austin rips off the Fembot's synthetic skin faceplate in the opening scene.

tropes.name: Rule of Three
tropes.html: Spoofed, where Mustafa, one of Dr. Evil's assassins, always answers a question truthfully the third time it's asked, because he can't stand being asked the same question three times. However, Mustafa will only answer if the same question is asked three consecutive times.

tropes.name: Sadistic Choice
tropes.html: Dr. Evil: Save the world... or save your girlfriend.

tropes.name: Sci-Fi Writers Have No Sense of Scale
tropes.html: When Dr.Evil threatens the President from his moon base, the General asks for permission to launch the U.S's nuclear arsenal to destroy the moon. In reality, the entire U.S nuclear arsenal going off at once would "only" make a crater about 10 km across, which wouldn't even be big enough to see with the naked eye from Earth, let alone destroy the entire thing.

tropes.name: Sequel Reset
tropes.html: "Wait a tick. That means I'm single again! Oh, behave!"

tropes.name: Sexy Surfacing Shot
tropes.html: In a parody of Honey Ryder's iconic scene in Dr. No, Felicity gracefully emerges on the beach in a white bikini...only to be followed by Austin doing the same, to both his and Felicity's confusion.

tropes.name: Shameless Fanservice Girl
tropes.html: Felicity. The majority of her outfits are skimpy and revealing (most likely part of her efforts to seduce Austin), and she has no problem flashing her panties while she and Austin tease a British Royal Guard, or showing her bare chest to an inept guard in order to lure him into her and Austin's cell.

tropes.name: Show Some Leg
tropes.html:
Felicity Shagwell bares her breasts to the one inept guard outside her and Austin's cell.
Felicity: What do you think of these, my man?
Guard: ...Mommy! (absentmindedly walks towards her and falls into the Lava Pit)

tropes.name: Sigil Spam
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's embossed logo can be found on nearly anything — makeup cases, motorized scooters, record turntables, even the doors of Dr. Evil's secret moon rocket.

tropes.name: Silence, You Fool!
tropes.html: "SILENCE! I will not tolerate your insolence!"

tropes.name: Smoking Hot Sex
tropes.html:
• Parodied at the beginning:
    Vanessa: Do you smoke after sex?
    Austin: I don't know, baby, I've never looked.
  • Felicity lights up after having sex with Fat Bastard.
  • Number Two and Number Two—which, technically, isn't cheating.

tropes.name: Snake Versus Mongoose
tropes.html: Dr. Evil says, "Austin Powers... he's the snake to my mongoose, or the mongoose to my snake. Either way it's bad. I don't know animals."

tropes.name: Snap Back
tropes.html:
• Austin had cleaned up his teeth by the end of the first movie, but upon arriving back in 1969, he finds that they have reverted back to their original unhygenic state.
  • While lusting after Felicity, Austin "grooms" himself like a cat, which gets his hair all messed up. But by the time he and Felicity meet face to face, his hair is back to normal.

tropes.name: Something Something Leonard Bernstein
tropes.html: Dr. Evil and Mini Me attempt to perform "What If God Was One Of Us" for their assosciates. Dr Evil can only remember the lyrics to the first two lines and resorts to singing "bloo-bloo-bloo" to fill in the rest.

tropes.name: Space Base
tropes.html: Another one of Dr. Evil's supervillain lairs. He seems to have every variation of this trope covered.

tropes.name: Squirrels in My Pants
tropes.html: During Austin's fight with Mini-Me on the moonbase, Mini-Me rips a hole in the crotch part of Austin's space suit and proceeds to climb inside. Austin initially panics when Mini-Me begins to crawl around inside his suit, but then begins to fidget around and giggle saying that it tickles. He then traps Mini-Me and then proceeds to eject him out the rear end of his suit through a nearby space toilet.

tropes.name: Straight Gay
tropes.html: The Beefeater remains still when Felicity kisses him on one of his cheeks. When Austin does the same to the other cheek, the guard turns toward Austin and cheekily smiles.

tropes.name: Summon Backup Dancers
tropes.html: Felicity does this by pressing a button on Austin's wall. The flat is immediately swarmed by hippies ready for a party.

tropes.name: Surveillance Station Slacker
tropes.html: An operative at a NATO Surveillance facility switches one of the screens he's supposed to be monitoring to The Jerry Springer Show.

tropes.name: Talk Show Appearance
tropes.html: Dr. Evil and Scott go on Jerry Springer as a subject of dysfunctional fathers. Dr. Evil eventually incites a riot by getting into a fight with a Klansman and causes a riot.

tropes.name: Talk to the Hand
tropes.html:
Dr. Evil does this, much to the U.S. President of 1969's confusion, as Dr. Evil's using '90s-era pop culture lines... in 1969.
Dr. Evil: Talk to the hand, 'cause the face don't wanna hear it anymore.
The President: What hand? Talk to your hand?

tropes.name: The Tease
tropes.html: Felicity. As she makes her way over to Austin, she briefly dances with two other guys before pushing them away. She also kisses a British Royal Guard on the cheek in hoping of making him move.

tropes.name: Testes Test
tropes.html: After the Fembot blows up in his face at the beginning of the movie, Austin moves his hands to his crotch, then faces the camera and announces, "Oh, thank God."

tropes.name: Threat Backfire
tropes.html: In a deleted scene, Felicity responds to Austin telling her she's "going the right way for a smacked bottom" with a flirty "I hope so!"

tropes.name: Timey-Wimey Ball
tropes.html:
By virtue of time-travel.
Austin: Wait a tick. Basil, if I travel back to 1969 and I was frozen in 1967, presumably, I could go back and visit my frozen self. But, if I'm still frozen in 1967, how could I have been unthawed in the '90s and traveled back to— [goes cross-eyed in confusion] Oh, no, I've gone cross-eyed.
Basil: I suggest you don't worry about those things and just enjoy yourself. [to the camera] That goes for you all, too.

tropes.name: Trailer Spoof
tropes.html: Had one related to The Phantom Menace.

tropes.name: Trip to the Moon Plot
tropes.html: The movie's third act is about Dr. Evil installing a giant "laser" on the Moon and Austin following him there to stop him.

tropes.name: Unstoppable Rage
tropes.html: After a Klansmen called Scott Evil a "freak", Dr. Evil ends up going ballistic. He ends up fighting even when being restrained by Steve Wilkos and the other members of security, and after seemingly calming down, he then rushes to attack him again (something that never happens on the Jerry Springer show). And then instigates a full-out brawl on the set. Eventually, he seems calmed down... until Jerry Springer tells security to get Dr. Evil out of the premises ("get this jerk out of here"), upon which his rage is reawakened, and he starts fighting with the host, eventually managing to smash a globe in the ensuing stage riot.

tropes.name: Vader Breath
tropes.html: Mocked when Dr. Evil's spacesuit is damaged, giving him a deeper voice and interrupted breathing. Naturally, he takes this moment to tell Austin he is his father. (He isn't really.)

tropes.name: Vocal Dissonance
tropes.html: At one point during the "Just The Two Of Us" musical number, the 2'8" Mini-Me sings a line in a very low baritone voice.

tropes.name: Wave-Motion Gun
tropes.html: The "Death Star" laser. (Ripoff!)

tropes.name: White Flag
tropes.html: Austin waves one when under fire by the Fembot in the opening scene.

tropes.name: Why Won't You Die?
tropes.html: Austin asks this verbatim of Robin Swallows, who shrugs off a lot of lethal attacks.

tropes.name: Writers Cannot Do Math
tropes.html:
• Mini-Me is described as being "one-eighth" Dr. Evil's size. But he's clearly closer to a third of the doctor's size.
  • Fat Bastard is said to weigh a "metric ton". For reference, that would be around 2000 lbs. He may be big, but he doesn't look anywhere near that big.
  • Austin is stated to have traveled back ten minutes in order to save Felicity, despite the fact that those events were closer to five minutes prior.

tropes.name: You Put the "X" in "XY"
tropes.html:
Invked by Austin himself.
Robin Swallows: Tell me, Mr. Powers: Do you swing?
Austin: Are you kidding, baby? I put the "Grr" in "Swinger", baby!"

tropes.name: And the Adventure Continues
tropes.html: Scott becomes the new Dr. Evil, and is apparently slightly more crazy, meaning the Powers family will have many more adventures to come.

tropes.name: Antagonist Title
tropes.html: Being a spoof of the Bond movies, Goldmember is used in place of Goldfinger as the title. Goldmember is indeed the antagonist, just not the only one.

tropes.name: As Long as It Sounds Foreign
tropes.html: Fook Yu, Fook Mi, and Mr. Roboto are not authentic Japanese names.

tropes.name: Big Bad Duumvirate
tropes.html: Dr. Evil teams up with Goldmember against Austin Powers.

tropes.name: Bowdlerize
tropes.html: In-universe, this was the case for Dr. Evil's "It's a Hard Knock Life" music video: Nudity was censored, and Dr. Evil's curse words were edited, radio edit-style.

tropes.name: Bread, Eggs, Milk, Squick
tropes.html:
Austin's "Things to Do Before I Die" checklist:
Become International Man of Mystery.
Save World From Certain Doom.
Find True Love.
Go To Outer Space.
Travel Through Time, Backward and Forward.
Be Cryogenically Frozen.
Catch Dr. Evil in the First Act.
Threesome with Japanese Twins.
Earn Daddy's Respect.

tropes.name: Breaking Old Trends
tropes.html:
Several elements shown in the previous two movies are absent here.
  • There are no Laugh-In-inspired scene transitions.
  • This movie lacks a scene where one of Dr. Evil's Mooks is killed, and Austin launches into a Hurricane of Puns revolving around the circumstances of the death.
  • Austin's Union Jack briefs don't appear.

tropes.name: Breast Attack
tropes.html: Austin subjects Fat Bastard to a double purple nurple during their brief fight.

tropes.name: Cameo Cluster
tropes.html: The opening is full of famous people playing themselves on the set of an In-Universe Austin Powers movie, which is being directed by Steven Spielberg and stars Tom Cruise, Gwyneth Paltrow, Kevin Spacey, and Danny DeVito, with Quincy Jones and Britney Spears (or a fembot thereof) doing the music.

tropes.name: Captain Obvious
tropes.html: Goldmember states the obvious when Dr. Evil starts giving Scott preferential treatment: "It's a power struggle." and "The tiny one can't take the hint."

tropes.name: Casting Gag
tropes.html: Harry Palmer himself, Michael Caine, appears as Nigel Powers.

tropes.name: Compressed Hair
tropes.html: After swimming to Dr. Evil's submarine Foxxy removes her swimcap to reveal short-looking hair. She shakes her head and it explodes, via a cut to Austin, into her usual enormous afro.

tropes.name: Consulting a Convicted Killer
tropes.html: After Austin learns that his father, Nigel, has been kidnapped and the only clue is that the crew of his yacht have had their genitalia painted gold, Austin visits Dr. Evil, who is being held in captivity in a cell much like Hannibal Lecter's, to find out who is responsible. Dr. Evil reveals to Austin that Goldmember is behind the abduction.

tropes.name: Continuity Nod
tropes.html: At the end of the first movie, Basil tells Austin that he will be knighted. Early on in this film, Austin is finally knighted.

tropes.name: Conveyor Belt o' Doom
tropes.html:
Parodies a very similar scene from Goldfinger with Austin's dad strapped to a device that moves him genitals-first towards a container pouring molten gold.
Goldmember: Your fajah is about to have an unfortunate smelting accident!

tropes.name: Daddy Didn't Show
tropes.html: Nigel Powers had a tendency for this, to the point Austin starts singing "Daddy Wasn't There", quoted atop that article.

tropes.name: Daddy Issues
tropes.html:
Austin responds to accusations of having "Daddy Issues" with this:
Austin: "Nothing could be My Father from the truth. For me this is a Dad issue....Dead! Dad! Deadbeat dad! Daddy didn't love me!"

tropes.name: Dark Horse Victory
tropes.html: As shown in a Flashback, Dr. Evil was actually the favorite to win the prestigious "International Man of Mystery" position at the secret agent academy. But despite this, Austin ended up receiving that honor instead.

tropes.name: Dead Partner
tropes.html: Foxxy Cleopatra had a partner who was killed by Goldmember, and is determined to bring the villain to justice for it.

tropes.name: Denser and Wackier
tropes.html: Goldmember relies less on parodies of the spy genre and more on broad humor, celebrity cameos and pop culture references that were trending in 2002.

tropes.name: Did I Just Say That Out Loud?
tropes.html:
Austin's got a problem separating his inner and outer voices. The Mole's facial blemishes prove just irresistible.
Austin: MOLE!

tropes.name: Didn't We Use This Joke Already?
tropes.html:
When they reuse the rocket-joke from the second movie.
Ozzy: These filmmakers are just [bleep] boobs!
Kelly: What do you mean, Dad?
Ozzy: Well, they're usin' the same [bleep] jokes they did in the last Austin Powers movie.

tropes.name: DreamWorks Face
tropes.html: The Dr. Evil giant submarine has one. Of course it's based on Dr. Evil's quirk of doing the same thing.

tropes.name: Dude, Not Funny!
tropes.html: Said In-Universe by Austin in regards to his father writing off Austin's quite legitimate complaints about his parenting skills with a joke.

tropes.name: Dull Surprise
tropes.html: The street-market shopper (Fred Stoller) who appears in the third section of the montage ("Are they nice and firm?") has this reaction to the satellite's coming into view.

tropes.name: Even the Subtitler Is Stumped
tropes.html: When Austin reunites with his father, in order to prevent the two American women who were keeping tabs on them from knowing what they are talking about, they opt to discus the details in English English, and communicate entirely in increasingly more nonsensical Cockney slang. The subtitler eventually gives up.

tropes.name: Everyone Went to School Together
tropes.html: It is revealed that Austin, Dr. Evil, Number Two and Basil all went to the secret agent academy at the same time (with Austin and Dr. Evil even sharing a dormitory).

tropes.name: Evil Diva
tropes.html: Britney Spears in the opening sequence, whom confidently rivals Austin in a dance battle, and reveals herself to be a Fembot assassin.

tropes.name: Expository Hairstyle Change
tropes.html: Not actually plot-driven, but Foxxy Cleopatra's hairstyle changes in virtually every new scene she's in.

tropes.name: Faceship
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's sub is modeled after him.

tropes.name: Fake Film Intro
tropes.html: The film opens with an action scene where the series' main characters have now been suspiciously recast - Austin Powers is portrayed by Tom Cruise, Dr. Evil by Kevin Spacey and Mini Me by Danny DeVito. It then cuts to a sound stage, revealing that the opening is just part of an in-universe Austin Powers movie being directed by Steven Spielberg.

tropes.name: Fake-Out Opening
tropes.html: The movie opens with a scene from a film within the film about Austin's life.

tropes.name: Flanderization
tropes.html:
Especially evident in Austinpussy (the movie-within-a-movie in Goldmember).
John Travolta as Goldmember: Hey, assholes! Do I have time for a last smoke and a pancake or what!?

tropes.name: Flashback Cut
tropes.html:
• There's a brief cut back to Dr. Evil's "Not So Different" Remark from the first movie.
  • Austin has one when Mini-Me flashes the "peace" symbol. He did this only to give him the finger and kick Austin in the face.

tropes.name: Freeze-Frame Bonus
tropes.html: The email Austin gets reads "Dear Customer: You are being sent a new credit card by FedEx because your old one was hacked while you were browsing iPods on eBay. Sincerely, Your Bank."

tropes.name: Freudian Slip
tropes.html:
• Austin repeatedly saying "dad" or "father" instead of other words.
Dr. Evil: Uh oh! Somebody's got some daddy issues!
Austin: Nothing could be my father from the truth.
Dr. Evil: Oop... you said "my father."
Austin: No I dadn't!
Dr. Evil: HOW!
Austin: Didn't! Did not!
Dr. Evil: Shappah!
Austin: For me, this is a dad issue.
Dr. Evil: Oop.
Austin: Dead issue! Dead... dead dad! Deadbeat dad! Daddy didn't love me!
  • Austin suffers from a similiar situation with Number Three.
Austin: Nice to mole you-meet you! Nice to meet your mole. ...Moley, moley, moley, moley!

tropes.name: Fun with Subtitles
tropes.html:
Mr. Roboto, when talking to Austin Powers and Foxxy Cleopatra, speaks in subtitles. With the series's usual No Fourth Wall comedy, the white objects in Mr. Roboto's room obscure some of his subtitles which are mistaken for much dirtier phrases until they are clarified. This is promptly Lampshaded by Austin Powers after Mr. Roboto reveals he can speak English the entire time.
Austin: Yeah, why don't you? That way I wouldn't misread the subtitles making it seem like you are saying things which are dirty. [looks to camera]

tropes.name: Great Escape
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's escape from normal prison involves starting a Prison Riot to cover the escape. He was able to manipulate the prison's populace after demonstrating how, you know, evil he is.

tropes.name: Gross-Up Close-Up
tropes.html: Whenever Number Three appears, there is always a zoom-in on his gigantic mole. He even twitches it a little...

tropes.name: Hair Reboot
tropes.html: Foxxy Cleopatra's hair goes from a fairly flat style from being wet to her full-out Funny Afro after she shakes her head.

tropes.name: Help Mistaken for Attack
tropes.html: Austin returns to his hotel room to find Mini-Me grinning at him while holding up a letter opener. The audience knows that Mini-Me is here because he defected from Dr. Evil (the "help") and that he was just using the letter opener to open some mail, but Austin immediately reads it as an ambush (the "attack") and gives him a sound thrashing.

tropes.name: Hypocritical Humor
tropes.html: There's two things Nigel Powers can't stand: "people who are intolerant of other people's cultures...and the Dutch!"

tropes.name: Ignore the Disability
tropes.html:
Number Three's mole. Around it, everyone feels inclined to unintentionally make stupid puns. "Why, thank yo— MOLE!!!" "Moley, moley, moley, moley, moley!"
  • Later defied when Number Three tells Austin to just get it out of his system. Austin gladly obliges.

tropes.name: Indignant Slap
tropes.html: Upon reuniting with Foxxy Cleopatra, Foxxy uses a random disco man as a cover to talk to Austin. In the middle of their conversation, Foxxy/Disco Man slaps Austin out of the blue, calling out Austin for not contacting her for 8 years.

tropes.name: Irony
tropes.html: Number Three lampshades this, noting that he is a mole who happens to have a rather large mole on his face.

tropes.name: Knighting
tropes.html: Austin gets knighted after catching Dr. Evil. Goes from being a cool moment to a sad one when his father doesn't show up.

tropes.name: Lame Pun Reaction
tropes.html: Dr. Evil: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to my submarine lair. It's long, hard and full of seamen! [nobody laughs] Nothing? Not even a titter?

tropes.name: Lawyer-Friendly Cameo
tropes.html: While the group are pursuing Goldmember, Nigel's car crashes into a float that looks like Godzilla, but due to international copyright laws, isn't actually Godzilla.

tropes.name: Medium Awareness
tropes.html:
Austin uses the subtitles to understand Japanese. What makes it funny is that the white subtitles are sometimes placed in front of white items, resulting in the subtitles looking entirely lewd.
Mr. Roboto: Why don't I just, uh, speak in English?
Austin: Yes, that would be helpful! Then we wouldn't continue to misread your subtitles, making it seem that you're saying things that are dirty! [cracks smile just before camera cuts away]

tropes.name: Mook Chivalry
tropes.html: "Look, here's how it goes, you attack me one at a time and I knock you out with one punch, okay? Go."

tropes.name: Moonwalk Dance
tropes.html: Scott Evil performs a moonwalk just before the end credits.

tropes.name: Never the Selves Shall Meet
tropes.html: Austin and Dr. Evil travel back in time to feud in the seventies while their "past" selves during that era are still in cryogenic suspension.

tropes.name: Nominal Importance
tropes.html:
Nigel Powers talks one of Dr. Evil's minions out of attacking him by pointing this out.
Nigel Powers: Have you any idea how many anonymous henchmen I've killed? Look at you! You don't even have a name tag! You've got no chance. Why don't you just fall down?
[the henchman falls down]

tropes.name: Not Even Bothering with the Accent
tropes.html: Tom Cruise uses his British accent while playing Austin in the In-Universe movie based on Austin's adventures.

tropes.name: Notzilla
tropes.html:
Lampshaded with two Japanese men running from a monster statue that vaguely resembles Godzilla during the car chase in Japan:
Japanese Man 1: RUUUUN!!! IT'S GODZILLA!
Japanese Man 2: It looks like Gojira, but due to international copyright laws, it's not.
Japanese Man 1: STILL, WE SHOULD RUN LIKE IT IS GODZILLA!
Japanese Man 2: [glances at the camera] Though it isn't.

tropes.name: Overt Rendezvous
tropes.html: Austin and Foxxy Cleopatra meet on a public bench, but with a man (Nathan Lane) sitting in between them, who moves his lips without speaking while Foxxy is the one actually talking. This way, to any outsider, it looks like Austin and the man are the only ones having a conversation.

tropes.name: Parental Neglect
tropes.html: Nigel was absent for most of the major events in Austin's life, including his graduation from secret agent academy.

tropes.name: Pixellation
tropes.html: Used on a woman's bare breasts in the "Hard Knock Life" music video.

tropes.name: Precision F-Strike
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's response to being caught in the first act, before even getting started on his Evil Plan, is simply "... shit."

tropes.name: Pretty Fly for a White Guy
tropes.html: Dr. Evil and Mini-Me performing a music video to the tune of "It's A Hard Knock Life" is all about parodying this. From the high and squeaky singing voice to the abrupt costume change, it is mockery.

tropes.name: Random Events Plot
tropes.html: The first half of the film. There's no reason given why Dr. Evil wants Nigel Powers abducted (while there are several plausible, justifiable reasons, he's never shown an interest in Austin's father before), why Nigel was taken to Goldmember's club in 1975 instead of just held somewhere in the present, or how Dr. Evil arranged his abduction from prison.note The opening scene implied Dr. Evil hadn't made contact with Goldmember yet. While it is possible that Number 2 or someone else could have contacted Goldmember and planned the abduction afterward, Dr. Evil either wouldn't know or had such a back-up plan in place already, and that just raises more questions. It is also unclear why Dr. Evil would reveal this to Austin when he could have sent him on a wild goose chase to somewhere else. The trope could be considered justified given the franchise is primarily a comedy, and Dr. Evil isn't known for his well thought-out plans, but it's still quite disjointed compared to the first two films. Once the action moves to Japan, things settle down into a more coherent plot structure.

tropes.name: Red Right Hand
tropes.html:
Goldmember's calling card is covering his victims' genitals in gold paint.
Goldmember: Dr. Evil, can I paint his [Nigel Powers'] yoo-hoo gold? It's kind of my thing, you know.
Dr. Evil: (pilots his mechanical chair up close to Goldmember) How about "No", you crazy Dutch bastard?!

tropes.name: Rent-a-Zilla
tropes.html: In a film series that parodies mostly James Bond films, a Notzilla appears.

tropes.name: Request for Privacy
tropes.html: Parodied. When Dr. Evil's son starts becoming evil himself, Dr. Evil shouts how it's getting a little crowded in the submarine deck they're all in and orders everyone to leave. Everyone starts getting up, but Dr. Evil then starts saying "Not you" followed by various people. By the time he's saying who doesn't have to leave, only Mini-Me hasn't been ordered to stay, making it apparent who Dr. Evil wants out of the room.

tropes.name: Retroactive Idiot Ball
tropes.html: This movie establishes that Austin and Dr. Evil went to the spy academy together. This makes Dr. Evil's attempt to pull a Luke, I Am Your Father on Austin in the previous movie (and Austin actually considering it to be a possibility) make them both look rather foolish in hindsight.

tropes.name: Reverse Polarity
tropes.html: Trying to stop the MIDAS asteroid from crashing into Earth and flooding it.

tropes.name: Self-Deprecation
tropes.html: Ozzy Osbourne: Boobs! These writers are a bunch of boobs!

tropes.name: Separated by a Common Language
tropes.html: There's a scene where Nigel Powers is talking about his sexual exploits and Austin requests that they speak in "English" English in front of the Americans. The proceeding conversation has subtitles. (But not all of it.)

tropes.name: Show Within a Show
tropes.html: Austinpussy, originally the intended title of this installment (a parody of Octopussy), which they couldn't get past the censors. It was directed by Steven Spielberg and starred Tom Cruise as Austin, Gwyneth Paltrow as the Bond Girl, Kevin Spacey as Dr. Evil, Danny DeVito as Mini-Me, and John Travolta as Goldmember.

tropes.name: Sir Swears-a-Lot
tropes.html: In a parody of late '90s/early 00s rap, one of the verses in Dr. Evil's "Hard Knock Life" rap is nearly completely censored from the amount of swearing.

tropes.name: Sound-Effect Bleep
tropes.html: Utilized during the cutaway to the Osbournes.

tropes.name: Sparing the Final Mook
tropes.html: When taken before Dr. Evil and Goldmember, Nigel effortlessly knocks out two mooks, then notices a third and final mook, who is obviously scared of him. Nigel decides to take it easy on the third guy, telling him to just act like Nigel knocked him out too and nobody will hold it against him. The mook quickly goes along with it.

tropes.name: Stealth Pun
tropes.html: The movie-within-a-movie has Mini-Me firing off an M-249 machine gun, also known as the "Minimi".

tropes.name: Surprisingly Realistic Outcome
tropes.html: When Mini-Me defects to MI 6, Austin finds him in his room holding letter opener and assumes he's been sent to assassinate him. Mini-Me attempts to convince Austin he's on his side now by giving the peace sign. Austin initially believes him but then remembers Mini-Me giving him the peace sign before pulling his I Surrender, Suckers! trick during their last encounter and declares "I'm not falling for that again!" and charging at him.

tropes.name: Swapped Roles
tropes.html: In the previous movie, Dr. Evil showed blatant favoritism to Mini-Me over Scott. In this movie, Dr. Evil and Scott's relationship has greatly improved and Mini-Me finds himself being phased out of Dr. Evil's inner circle, resulting in him turning on the villainous doctor and siding with the good guys.

tropes.name: Sweet Tooth
tropes.html: Mini Me is shown to have a near-obsessive love of chocolate, Dr. Evil noting that the food is like "catnip for clones".

tropes.name: Take That!
tropes.html: Number Two tells Dr. Evil that he's found a way for them to make plenty of legitimate money while still retaining the "ethics" of an evil organization: becoming a Hollywood talent agency.

tropes.name: Taught by Experience
tropes.html: Played for dramatic irony with Austin when Mini-Me tries to defect (and Austin thinks the clone's trying to kill him again). When Mini-Me tries to peacefully surrender, Austin (who's been left out of the loop about the defection) doesn't believe him. After all, this is ''exactly'' what Mini-Me did on the Moon Base in the previous film before kicking the crap out of Austin. So, Austin not unreasonably thinks he's being suckered again and refuses to fall for this stunt twice (and thus doesn't realize it's not an act).

tropes.name: Totem Pole Trench
tropes.html: Invoked by Austin and Mini-Me during the infiltration of Dr. Evil's sub (albeit with Austin being the one on top).

tropes.name: Tough Room
tropes.html: Nobody laughs at Dr. Evil's "long and hard and full of seamen" joke, prompting him to say, "Tough sub."

tropes.name: Tractor Beam
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's plan this time around is to use a tractor beam to cause the Midas-22 asteroid to crash into Earth.

tropes.name: Twin Threesome Fantasy
tropes.html: Austin and the Japanese girls.

tropes.name: Ungrateful Bastard
tropes.html: Nigel shows little regard to Austin for saving him from an "unfortunate smelting accident", instead pointing out that Goldmember is getting away because of him.

tropes.name: Vocal Dissonance
tropes.html: Subverted in the Studio 69 scene, when Foxxy uses a man like a ventriloquist's dummy to speak to Austin covertly. At first glance, it seems like the guy is speaking with a sexy black woman's voice.

tropes.name: Wham Line
tropes.html:
Near the end when Nigel prevents Austin from shooting Dr. Evil:
Austin: Dr. Evil's not your son! I am!
Nigel: You both are.

tropes.name: What Happened to the Mouse?
tropes.html:
• Mr. Bigglesworth isn't seen at all.
  • Austin's Bond Girl from Shagged, Felicity Shagwell, is no where to be seen, nor is any explanation given for her absence. Looks like Basil was right when he said it wasn't meant to be.

tropes.name: Who's on First?
tropes.html: The Asian twins Fook Mi and Fook Yu. Austin is quite confused at first, but they evidently run into this problem on a regular basis and have their names on their bakcpacks.

tropes.name: Wire Fu
tropes.html: Parodied. Fat Bastard tries to use a Wire Fu attack on Austin (to the point of being visibly held up by wires and calling attention to the people in the background holding him up.) One of the wires breaks halfway through, though, and he's just left dangling in the air.

tropes.name: Yank the Dog's Chain
tropes.html:
Austin is bummed that his dad didn't attend his knighting ceremony. Later, Basil exposition informs Austin that his father was kidnapped:
Austin: Heavy, man. [perks up] OH! So that's why he wasn't at my knighting ceremony!
Basil: No, actually, he was kidnapped after you were knighted.
Austin: Ah.

tropes.name: Your Princess Is in Another Castle!
tropes.html: Austin gets Dr. Evil arrested in the very beginning, making it clear that something will inevitably go wrong. Dr. Evil even does a musical number pointing this out ("Austin caught me in the first act/it's all backwards, what's with that"?).

entries.reason: As International Man of Mystery

tropes.name: Actor Allusion
tropes.html:
• A recurring Mission Control character (whose name is revealed to be Johnson to fit the running gag about a phallic rocket) is played by Clint Howard, mocking his role as a NASA technician in Apollo 13.
  • Austin's line about "controlling the VOLUME OF [HIS] VOICE" in the first film originated in a SNL sketch a few years prior, in which Myers played a British film-show host.
  • When Dr. Evil drops Mini-Me and he hops back up, Dr. Evil exclaims "And he's okay!" just like Myers did about Stacey in Wayne's World.
  • Nigel Powers drives a modified Mini Cooper for his spy car, a vehicle strongly associated with Michael Caine's The Italian Job (1969).
  • The therapist leading the father-son support group is Carrie Fisher - whose most famous role is the daughter of one of the most famous evil fathers in all of fiction.

tropes.name: Affectionate Parody
tropes.html:
• The first is mostly a parody of James Bond knockoffs and sixties culture in general. This is mostly continued in the second one, with various bits of sci-fi thrown in with all the time travel abuse.
  • While the first one may be best-known for its spoofing of Bond films, its storyline actually owes a lot to Demolition Man as well, with the protagonist being brought out of cryogenic suspension to deal with an old enemy, and having to adapt to a major case of culture shock along the way. The way in which Austin is thawed out is also very similar to how Sylvester Stallone's character gets thawed out in that film.
  • The third movie parodies Blaxploitation movies and the Austin Powers franchise itself.

tropes.name: Air Quotes
tropes.html:
• Dr. Evil does this while explaining one of his evil plans to his staff, using air quotes where the text shows quotes.
    Dr. Evil: Back in the '60s I developed a weather-changing machine which was in essence a sophisticated heat beam which we called a "laser". Using these "lasers", we punch a hole in the protective layer around the world, which we call the "ozone layer".
  • The fact that Dr. Evil seems unable to say the word "laser" without using this trope becomes a Running Gag.
    Dr. Evil: In exactly six hours, the moon will move in its orbit around the Earth, bringing Washington D.C. within range of my giant "laser". Begin "laser" ignition sequence!
  • In a deleted scene available on DVD, Dr. Evil claims that he invented finger quotes.

tropes.name: All There in the Manual
tropes.html:
The official guide book, The World of Austin Powers, fills in quite a few characters' backstories and other such things.
  • Austin's cryogenic chamber is shown in a single small room in the second movie, rather than the large vault seen in the first. The World of Austin Powers explains that after Austin's mojo was successfully stolen, it was decided to move Austin's body to the celebrity vault, on the grounds that it would be more visible and thus better protected.
  • Basil's entire wardrobe consists of hidden weaponry, such as an acid-firing buttonhole, and creases in his trousers sharp enough to cut through flesh and bone.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Martial Arts
tropes.html: Played for comedy with Austin's "judo" skills. For the unaware, judo is a martial art almost entirely based around grappling and throws, with strikes being outright banned in official competitions and formal sparring. Naturally, this means that Austin throws out almost nothing but strikes, punctuating them with things like "Judo chop!" and "Judo kick!"

tropes.name: Aside Glance
tropes.html:
Frequently follows some of Austin's particularly painful jokes.
Austin: [upon face with Dr. Evil's bare buttocks] You know, Dr. Evil, I used to think you were crazy.
Dr. Evil: I know.
Austin: But now I can see your nuts. [turns to face the camera] A-thank you!

tropes.name: Astonishingly Appropriate Interruption
tropes.html:
• In the second movie, Dr. Evil's... phallic... rocket inspires a whole chain of people getting cut off just as they're about to mention it looks like a giant
    Female Fan: Woody! Woody Harrelson? Can I have your autograph?
  • In the third film, the strange object resembles breasts instead. The gag runs for a while and then is duly Lampshaded (by Ozzy Osbourne, no less).

tropes.name: Bait-and-Switch Silhouette
tropes.html:
• In the second movie, guards see what seems to be Felicity Shagwell removing various different objects out of Austin's ass. It's actually a bag on a table next to Austin, who's hunched over a map.
  • In the third movie, a mook believes he sees an impossible silhouette of a man with a small arm for a penis, who shakes hands with it and feeds it before giving birth. It turns out to be Austin, Mini-Me, some tubing and an apple.

tropes.name: Better than a Bare Bulb
tropes.html:
• Every Bond trope from Death Trap to Bond Girl is ubiquitously pointed out and made fun of.
  • By Goldmember, they frequent hang a lampshade on their own jokes, old and new. Goldmember implies that his weird accent automatically makes him funny and makes sure everyone notices his "subtle" references to music lyrics. Austin and Mr. Roboto point out that they could just speak English to avoid confusion, and Ozzy's dialogue under Didn't We Use This Joke Already?.

tropes.name: Big Bad
tropes.html: Dr. Evil is the evil mastermind for most of the trilogy.

tropes.name: Big "NO!"
tropes.html:
• A guard while Austin is driving toward him with a steamroller (actually a "STOOOOOOOOOP"), and Austin himself before leaping to push the underground drill's abort button. The steamroller bit goes into Overly Long Gag territory because the Mook stands there for a full 15 seconds shouting "STOOOOOP!" before the steamroller slowly crushes him.
  • Both Austin and his past self call out "No!" (in slow motion) while trying to catch Austin's mojo.

tropes.name: Binocular Shot
tropes.html:
• The first movie includes one as Austin and Vanessa scope out Virtucon.
  • The second movie features two such shots, one when Felicity observes Austin meeting Robin Swallows, and another when Austin scopes out Dr. Evil's headquarters.

tropes.name: Blissfully Horrific Backstory
tropes.html:
When Dr. Evil has to go to therapy with his son Scott, he recounts his profoundly bizarre (adoptive, though he didn't know it yet) childhood with an utterly deadpan tone, clearly seeing nothing wrong with it.
The details of my life are quite inconsequential. Very well, where do I begin? My father was a relentlessly self-improving boulangerie owner from Belgium with a low-grade narcolepsy and a penchant for buggery. My mother was a fifteen-year-old French prostitute named Chloë with webbed feet. My father would womanize, he would drink. He would make outrageous claims like he invented the question mark. Sometimes he would accuse chestnuts of being lazy. The sort of general malaise that only the genius possess and the insane lament. My childhood was typical. Summers in Rangoon, luge lessons. In the spring we'd make meat helmets. When I was insolent I was placed in a burlap bag and beaten with reeds—pretty standard really. At the age of twelve I received my first scribe. At the age of fourteen a Zoroastrian named Wilma ritualistically shaved my testicles. There really is nothing like a shorn scrotum. It's breathtaking—I suggest you try it.

tropes.name: The Body Parts That Must Not Be Named
tropes.html:
Parodied.
  • When Dr. Evil flies his phallic rocket, everyone says something along the lines of "It looks like a big..." but is cut off by the next person, saying a synonym for penis in an unrelated concept.
  • The third movie has a similar sequence regarding people reacting to a satellite that looks like a pair of breasts falling out of orbit.

tropes.name: Bond One-Liner
tropes.html: Spoofed. A lot.

tropes.name: Bond Villain Stupidity
tropes.html: Used and lampshaded, most notably in the scene where Scott asks "Why Don't You Just Shoot Him?"

tropes.name: Borrowed Catchphrase
tropes.html:
• When Austin tells Vanessa that he's just fine with being a one-woman man if she wants him to be, Vanessa warmly uses his "Behave" line.
  • At the end of the third movie, Dr. Evil says "Yeah baby!" Everyone stares blankly at him, and he adds: "No? Just trying it on."

tropes.name: Brick Joke
tropes.html:
• In the first film, Austin claims to hate Carnies (or "circus folk") because they "smell like cabbage". Two films later, his father is ambushed by Mini-Me. His response? "I thought I smelled cabbage."
  • When the first movie begins Austin has just propositioned a pair of Japanese twins before he's called away to save the world, much to his dismay. Two movies later (again) the list above appears.
  • In the first movie, Dr. Evil says to Austin that they are 'not so different' (which also doubles as a comedic Actor Allusion), and in the second Dr. Evil pulls a Luke, I Am Your Father moment to Austin seemingly just to mess with him. In the third movie it is revealed that they are brothers.

tropes.name: The Brute
tropes.html: Random Task is the primary muscle and hitman (Fat Bastard takes over this role from him in the second film).

tropes.name: Calling Your Attacks
tropes.html: "Judo X!" and Foxxy's "Shazam!!"

tropes.name: The Cameo
tropes.html: Many in every movie. The first had two (Christian Slater and Rob Lowe) cut in North America but present everywhere else. The second has among others, two for the Astonishingly Appropriate Interruption (and the third has another lampshading how this joke is a repeat). The third opens with a fake Austin Powers movie filled with these.

tropes.name: Carnival of Killers
tropes.html: Among the various killers hired by Dr. Evil are an Asian man named Random Task who uses his shoe to kill people, an Irishman who strangles people with a bracelet with lucky charms on it, and a vaguely Middle-Eastern man who angers Dr. Evil but will just not die.

tropes.name: Cartwright Curse
tropes.html: Played for laughs throughout the series in parody of James Bond's habit of hooking up with a new beautiful woman in each movie who disappears with little to no fanfare in the next. Vanessa is revealed to be a Fembot to re-bachelor Austin at the beginning of the second movie with little recognition from the characters, and Felicity just disappears.note A scene was planned to explain her disappearance, but it was set aside once they got all the cameos confirmed.

tropes.name: Catching Up on History
tropes.html: After being frozen for 30 years, Austin spends some time watching TV to try and learn about what he missed, including the moon landings.

tropes.name: Catchphrase
tropes.html: Austin's is "Yeah, baby!" or "Yeah, baby, yeah!". They're used both as an excited exclamation and a lascivious come on (sometimes simultaneously).

tropes.name: Characterization Marches On
tropes.html: In the first movie, Austin showed little regard for his poor oral hygiene, reacting with confusion when Vanessa tried to introduce him to modern dental products (and annoyance when she seemed to be doing so a second time), only cleaning up his teeth after a Time Skip. In the second movie, learning that travelling back to the sixties has somehow reverted his teeth back to their former state leads Austin to self-consciously try to hide them.

tropes.name: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome
tropes.html:
• Dr. Evil's minions, Alotta Fagina and Random Task aren't mentioned after the first movie. The former could have been killed in the lair explosion but so should have Frau and Scott.
    • It's entirely likely that, given he was taken down in Austin & Vanessa's hotel room, Random Task was simply sent to prison.
  • Felicity Shagwell in the third movie.
  • Mr. Bigglesworth (and Mini-Mr. Bigglesworth) is also absent in the third movie.

tropes.name: Continuity Snarl
tropes.html:
• Frau and Scott appear in the second movie despite supposedly being caught in Dr. Evil's lair exploding. Number Two appears as well despite being incinerated near the end by Dr. Evil himself (an alternate ending that is mostly full of continuity errors states that he escaped the fire pit alive).
  • At the end of the first movie, Basil informs Austin that he is going to be knighted for saving the world. The third movie, taking place years later, shows Austin being knighted for finally capturing Dr. Evil.

tropes.name: Cool Car
tropes.html:
• Austin's preferred mode of transport is a Jaguar convertible painted in the colors of the Union Jack (which he dubs "Shaguar" in the second movie).
  • The time machine Austin uses in the second movie is a volkswagon convertible painted in psychadelic colors.
  • Felicity drives a 1965 Corvette convertible painted in the colors of the America flag.
  • Nigel's car is a Mini Cooper, to his son's surprise.
    Austin: Your spy car's a Mini?
    Nigel: It's not the size, mate; It's how you use it.

tropes.name: Creepy Hairless Animal
tropes.html: Dr. Evil has a Right-Hand Cat named Mr. Bigglesworth, who loses all of his hair during a cryogenics accident. Before the accident he's played by a white Persian cat, after it he's played by a Sphinx.

tropes.name: Culture Equals Costume
tropes.html:
• When Dr. Evil calls up the United Nations Secret Meeting Room to give his ultimatum during the first movie, many of the occupants are dressed in costumes indicating their native countries (two Japanese are dressed as a geisha and a sumo wrestler, a British representative is wearing a Beefeater costume, a Spaniard is dressed as a matador, etc.). One of the characters (presumably an American) is dressed as a cowboy.
  • When we first see Fat Bastard he's wearing a tam o'shanter and a kilt while bagpipe music plays.

tropes.name: Damsel in Distress
tropes.html: Both Vanessa and Felicity are captured offscreen and held hostage in order to raise the stakes in the climactic showdown.

tropes.name: Dancing on a Bus
tropes.html: Austin dances with Miss Kensington on a double-decker bus as Burt Bacharach plays the piano.

tropes.name: Dancing Theme
tropes.html: During the opening titles of each movie, Austin dances to the theme tune of the films with supposedly random bystanders.

tropes.name: Deconstructive Parody
tropes.html:
The series is a parody of James Bond specifically, and the counter-culture movement of the 60s in general. Mostly, it does this with a wink and a nod by showing the Surprisingly Realistic Outcomes of trying to be either a super-spy or a supervillain, or how Austin is a Fish out of Temporal Water.
  • In the first movie, Dr. Evil wants sharks with Frickin' Laser Beams attached to their heads. Number Two informs Dr. Evil that they couldn't get any, because sharks ending up on the endangered species list meant that "it would have taken months to clear up all the red tape".
  • In the second movie, Dr. Evil demands one hundred billion dollars from the United States government in 1969. The president, while laughing, informs Dr. Evil that such an amount of money doesn't even exist.
  • The third movie averts You Can't Thwart Stage One by having Austin thwart Dr. Evil at Stage One, catching him in the act of announcing his Evil Plan and sending him to jail right then and there.

tropes.name: Department of Redundancy Department
tropes.html:
• In the first movie: "Allow myself to introduce... myself."
  • In the second: "You're a very groovy baby... baby."
  • And in the third: "What do you know about my father's where... about... s?"

tropes.name: The Dragon
tropes.html: Number Two is responsible for running the evil empire on Dr.Evil's behalf.

tropes.name: Dressing as the Enemy
tropes.html: Once per movie, and Played for Laughs.

tropes.name: Energy Weapon
tropes.html: Frickin' Laser Beams attached to the heads of sharks. They're realistic lasers with continuous beams. (This is also the former Trope Namer of Slow Laser).

tropes.name: Epic Fail
tropes.html:
• Austin attempts to flip into his car near the end of the film... only to land crotch-first on the stick shift.
  • The first time Dr. Evil tries to time travel and just runs into the time machine without remembering to turn it on.
  • Austin gets ready to drive a time-travelling VW Bug into the future...but forgets that it's in reverse.

tropes.name: Euphemistic Names
tropes.html: Being an Affectionate Parody of the James Bond films, the Austin Powers films have at least one example of this in each film and it's Played for Laughs. Such examples include Number Two's companion Alotta Fagina, Austin's Love Interest in the second film Felicity Shagwell ("Shagwell by name, Shag very well by reputation"), Dr. Evil's spies Ivana Humpalot and Robin Swallows and an In-Universe film character named Dixie Normous.

tropes.name: Even Evil Has Standards
tropes.html:
Dr. Evil may be a Card-Carrying Villain, but even he has his limits.
  • He shuts down Fat Bastard mocking Austin over his sleeping with Felicity by stating that he doesn't want to think about Fat Bastard naked.
  • He is utterly weirded out by Goldmember's eccentric nature (and habit of eating his own skin).
  • When the newly-evil Scott lets his Evil Laugh get away from him, Dr. Evil is noticeably disturbed.

tropes.name: Everyone Went to School Together
tropes.html: Austin, Basil, Dr. Evil, and Number Two were all in Spy Academy together. Somehow.

tropes.name: Evil Genius
tropes.html: Frau Farbissina is responsible for things like the Fembots and the clones. Dr. Evil himself also counts while being combined with the Big Bad.

tropes.name: Evil Laugh
tropes.html: Spoofed massively. Often causes those trying to emulate Doctor Evil to fail hard. Overlaps with Leave the Camera Running in the first film. Dr. Evil and his minions share a bout of maniacal laughter... and then instead of cutting away at its peak, the camera keeps rolling as it slowly and awkwardly peters out.

tropes.name: Evil Plan
tropes.html: Each movie has one naturally, but of note is an early scene in the first movie. There Dr. Evil lists in detail two possible evil plans only to have Number Two tell him they already happened. So he shrugs and says 'Let's do what we always do: hijack nuclear weapons and hold the world hostage'.

tropes.name: Exty Years from Publication
tropes.html: International Man of Mystery starts in 1967, then moves forward to 1997. Reversed in The Spy Who Shagged Me, which starts in 1999 before heading toward 1969.

tropes.name: Fan Disservice
tropes.html: Fat Bastard whenever he tries and fails to come across as sexy and seductive.

tropes.name: Formally Named Pet
tropes.html: Mr. Bigglesworth.

tropes.name: Gag Penis
tropes.html:
• Aside from everything Nigel says about Mini-Me's endowments, there's the fact that when Mini-Me lowers his pants, there is an audible thump.
  • Goldmember has a gold...er, member.
  • The phallic-looking rocket in the second movie, inspiring an Overly Long Gag of bystanders reacting to it.

tropes.name: Girl of the Week
tropes.html: Every trope that applies to a Bond Girl applies to Austin's women.

tropes.name: Go-Go Enslavement
tropes.html: The goofy futuristic clothes Dr. Evil forces on Austin and Vanessa.

tropes.name: Good Pays Better
tropes.html: Played With. In every movie, Number Two will tell Doctor Evil that they're making a lot more money with legitimate business operations than evil plans. In response, Dr. Evil says "SILENCE, NUMBER TWO!" and then does the Evil Plan anyway. Virtucons' legitimate businesses might not qualify as "good", but they are much more morally neutral than what Dr Evil wants.

tropes.name: Groin Attack
tropes.html:
• Downplayed near the end of the first film. Austin leaps into his Jaguar, only to land with his groin hitting the stick shift. Once Vanessa gets into the car, she moves the shifter and accidentally hits Austin in the same tender area.
  • Mini-Me first kicks, then bites Austin in the junk in the second film, during their fight on the moon base. He kicks him there again during their brief fight in the third film.
    • Also in the third film, he accidentally sends a model meteor right into Dr. Evil's testicles. Way to go, A-hole!
  • Felicity pulls it off on Fat Bastard when she kicks him in the "mommy-daddy button" near the end of the second film, causing Austin to lecture her:
    Austin Powers: I don't care if he is evil, you don't give a man a shot in the pills. It's just not cricket, baby!
  • In the third film, Fat Bastard invokes this during his sumo wrestling match.
    Fat Bastard: You know what my favorite Helen Hunt movie is? Twister!

tropes.name: Groupie Brigade
tropes.html: Austin appearing in public usually tends to attract a screaming whorde.

tropes.name: The Guards Must Be Crazy
tropes.html: Spoofed and lampshaded without mercy.

tropes.name: Heel–Face Turn
tropes.html: Mini-Me, Dr. Evil, and Fat Bastard, as well. And maybe Frau and Number 2.

tropes.name: Highly Conspicuous Uniform
tropes.html: The silver suits worn by Dr. Evil and his henchmen.

tropes.name: Hoist by His Own Petard
tropes.html:
• Mini-Me pummels Austin for most of their fight on the moon. That is, until he crawls into Austin's spacesuit through the hole he just tore in it. This allows Austin to trap Mini-Me in the back and expel him through a nearby waste disposal unit.
  • Mini-Me's I Surrender, Suckers! stunt comes back to bite him in the ass in Goldmember when he defects for real and Austin (who was left out of the loop) thinks the clone's here to try to kill him again. When Mini-Me tries tries to peacefully surrender, Austin remembers what happened on the Moon Base and thinks Mini-Me's trying to sucker him again.

tropes.name: Hurricane of Puns
tropes.html: Once a movie, Austin will make one about a mook's death, and promptly told to shut up when he takes up minutes of screentime annoying his partner with the horrendous puns.

tropes.name: Imperial Stormtrooper Marksmanship Academy
tropes.html: Being a James Bond parody, of course the henchmen are horrible shots.

tropes.name: Jaw Drop
tropes.html:
• When Austin uses his mojo to turn the tables on the Fembots, one of them stares at him slack-jawed, on the verge of overload.
  • Several jaws drop (mostly those of women) when Austin makes his triumphant return to the sixties.
  • The first person Felicity dances with initially stares with slack-jawed awe at her beauty.
  • Austin's jaw drops with surprise and lust when Felicity effortlessly counters his attempt at flirting with her when they first meet, and again when he sees her in her Sexy Backless Outfit.
  • Several of Dr. Evil's guards' jaws hang open at the sight of the Bait-and-Switch Silhouette of Felicity appearing to be removing and reinserting objects from Austin's rear.

tropes.name: Joke Exhaustion
tropes.html: Whenever Austin offs a mook, he'll rattle off a list of incredibly lame Bond one liners about the nature of said mook's death. He generally has to be stopped by someone else before he'll move on. There is also a bunch of sexual euphemisms at the end.

tropes.name: Juggling Loaded Guns
tropes.html: Austin can be seen shaking his arms and blinking uncontrollably whenever he fires his gun. Mike Myers notes in the commentary that it was done only half-intentionally, as Mike himself had never fired a gun before.

tropes.name: Just Plane Wrong
tropes.html: Austin's shown to own a private Boeing 747, which has been preserved since he was frozen. Austin was frozen in 1967, the first 747 flew in 1969 and wouldn't be air certified until 1970.

tropes.name: Kick the Dog
tropes.html:
• When Austin attempts to counter Dr. Evil's forces taking Vanessa hostage by taking Scott hostage, Dr. Evil is indifferent. When the horrified Scott reminds his father that they just had a breakthrough in group, Dr. Evil announces that he had the group "liquidated" for being "insolent".
  • After Dr. Evil reveals to Austin that Felicity slept with Fat Bastard, Fat Bastard proceeds to mock both Austin (with a taunting "Boo-hoo") and Felicity (calling her "crap" in bed).
  • Nigel disregards Austin calling him out for his neglect, and makes a joke at his expense.

tropes.name: Kinky Spanking
tropes.html:
• A scene transition in the first movie depicts a member of Austin's band faux-spanking him.
  • A deleted scene from the second movie features Felicity swatting Austin's rear three times, to his clear delight.

tropes.name: Laugh with Me!
tropes.html:
• Dr. Evil doesn't like to make an Evil Laugh by himself.
  • Parodied in the last scene of the third movie where Scott laughs alone and desperately turns in every direction for someone to join in.

tropes.name: Licensed Pinball Table
tropes.html: Released in 2001, and based on the first two films. Click here for more.

tropes.name: "London, England" Syndrome
tropes.html: The Trope Namer was referring to this film series.

tropes.name: Luke, I Am Your Father
tropes.html:
• Gender-swapped in the second film, when Frau Farbissina admits she is Scott's mother.
  • Spoofed in the second with Dr. Evil and Austin.
  • Played straight in the third film, when it's revealed Austin and Dr. Evil are brothers.

tropes.name: Made of Iron
tropes.html: Mustafa, in the first two films (surviving being tipped into a furnace in the first film, only escaping with a broken leg after his car goes over a cliff in the second), and Robin Spitz-Swallows, also in the second film.

tropes.name: Male Gaze
tropes.html:
• In IMoM, our first view of Vanessa Kensington via a slow pan up her entire body.
  • During the chess scene, the camera pans down to Ivana Humpalot's chest as she squeezes her breasts together.
  • In a deleted scene from the second film, Austin shakes Robin Swallows by the hand really hard just to watch her cleavage bounce up and down.
  • Felicity Shagwell is introduced effortlessly catching the eyes of males as she makes her way over to Austin (with one such male openly staring at her chest).
  • After Felicity flirtatiously suggests that Austin has met his match in her, she walks away seductively. Austin can't keep his eyes off her.
  • Foxxy's introductory scene has Austin entranced.

tropes.name: A Man Is Always Eager
tropes.html: Austin quick to flirt and offer a chance of lovemaking with most women who cross his path. The second movie subverts this somewhat; while he openly flirts with both Robin and Felicity after losing his mojo, he balks at the idea of actually going to bed with Felicity, regretfully rejecting her.

tropes.name: Meeting-the-Parents Sequel
tropes.html: Austin's Father is introduced. Kind of odd that his dad is still alive, given how Austin is from the 60s, though the movie doesn't even bother to explain it.

tropes.name: "Metaphor" Is My Middle Name
tropes.html: Austin's full name is "Austin Danger Powers". When he was thawed in the first film, his effects were listed under his middle name.

tropes.name: Mini-Me
tropes.html: The character Mini-Me introduced in the second film is the Trope Namer, as he's a clone of Dr. Evil in "every way" except 1/8th his size.

tropes.name: Mood Whiplash
tropes.html:
• In the opening of the first movie, Dr. Evil eliminates his minions who have failed him... cue Austin dancing to Soul Bossa Nova.
  • In the extended version of the first film, every time Austin kills a Mook, the film immediately clips to about 30 seconds worth of the mook's mourning friends and family.
  • Given the silliness of the first film, Austin's speech to Dr. Evil about "if we'd known the consequences of our actions we'd have done things differently" referring to the Free Love era is actually straightforward and serious (and reflects real-world opinions of those who lived through the era).
  • In the second film, Austin mourns over Vanessa being a Fembot... until he realizes this means he's single again. OH BEHAVE! [cue Soul Boss Nova again!]
  • In the second and third films, Fat Bastard gives a heartfelt speech about his weight... then farts.

tropes.name: The '90s
tropes.html: The first two movies. The third one takes place in 2002.

tropes.name: No Fourth Wall
tropes.html:
• In the second film, Basil and Austin advise the audience not to think too hard about the time travel aspect of the story. Austin also introduces Burt Bacharach, Quincy Jones and Elvis Costello to the viewers.
  • In the third film, an obvious example is when Austin and Fat Bastard are fighting and Fat Bastard does "the ultimate wire-fighting maneuver", only for one of his wires to break.
  • Not to mention the numerous times when Austin looks directly at the camera when saying something. One example is during the Mr. Roboto scene. Austin, after misreading several subtitles for Mr. Roboto's dialogue, is pretty weirded out. Mr. Roboto says "Why don't I just speak English?" This leads to:
    Austin: Yeah, why don't you? That way I wouldn't misread the subtitles making it seem like you are saying things which are dirty. (Looks to camera)
  • Another camera look occurs when Austin is shot at on the ladder near the end and falls, pulling down Dr. Evil's pants to stop his fall. He says:
    Austin: You know, Dr. Evil, I used to think you were crazy.
    Dr. Evil: I know.
    Austin: But now I can see you're nuts. [looks at camera] Ah, thank you.

tropes.name: Noodle Incident
tropes.html:
• In the second movie, past Number Two claims that they've tried to steal Austin's mojo before.
  • After leaving Mr. Roboto's office, Austin comments that Mr. Roboto knows more than he was telling. Foxy replies "Tell me something I don't know", to which Austin says "I open-mouth kissed a horse once." Foxy replies "What?", and Austin says "That's something you don't know."

tropes.name: "Not So Different" Remark
tropes.html:
• Parodied in the first film. Dr. Evil tries this with Austin, claiming that the things Austin believes in are now considered "evil" by modern society.
  • Tried again by Dr. Evil in the third film. Although this instance seems to be a subtle foreshadowing of them finding out that they do have something in common - a father - at the end of the movie.

tropes.name: Offscreen Villain Dark Matter
tropes.html: Each movie begins with Number Two revealing a wildly successful business venture that he embarked on in Dr. Evil's absence. The funding for Dr. Evil's projects most likely comes from there.

tropes.name: Ooh, Me Accent's Slipping
tropes.html:
• There's a point during the Overly Long Gag of the evil laughing scene in the first film where Mike Myers reverts to his normal voice.
  • In the second film, when Austin asks Mustafa "Where is Dr. Evil hiding?", you can clearly hear Mike Myers' own voice. While portraying Fat Bastard, Myers occasionally slips into his Austin Powers accent, notably when Fat Bastard wants to eat Mini-Me ("Wait a minute, he kinda looks like a baby...").
  • Meyers notes in the commentary that Dr. Evil sounds pretty Canadian a few times in Goldmember, most of all with the line "I was adopted by frickin' Belgians, eh!"

tropes.name: Overly Long Gag
tropes.html:
The series lampshades, spoofs, and plays it straight as one of their overlong running gags is interrupted by a cameo from The Osbournes... who then turn out to be the part of it that brings it full circle.
  • Case in point, Austin's "evacuation" from the first movie.
  • Dr. Evil leads his underlings in an extended evil laugh, which goes on for several seconds until it awkwardly peters out.
