  • The near deaths of Mustafa and his crying out for help.
  • "Shh." "Zip it." "SCOTTY DON'T!"

tropes.name: Playing with a Trope
tropes.html: The entire purposes of the series, as it parodies, spins, exaggerates, lampshades, and puts an odd twist on everything from random dance scenes to celebrity cameos to under-the-credits scenes.

tropes.name: Preemptive "Shut Up"
tropes.html: Every time Scott points out the flaws in Dr. Evil's plans, Dr. Evil will throw a "Shh!" at him.

tropes.name: Pretty in Mink
tropes.html: The models in the second movie, and Austin wearing a pimp coat in the third.

tropes.name: Product Placement
tropes.html:
• International Man of Mystery. While Austin is catching up on events of the last thirty years (while he was a Human Popsicle), there are many empty cans of the Tab soft drink sitting on the table in front of him.
  • The minibar in Austin's Japanese hotel room has cans of Pepsi Twist.
  • In Goldmember, Austin uses a prominently placed MacBook. Also, contrasting his Jaguar that was renamed "Shaguar" from the beginning, his new VW Beetle sports its actual VW logo on the grill, and the camera lingers on it for a while when the car is introduced.

tropes.name: Punny Name
tropes.html: A lot of them, usually mocking James Bond characters. Let's see, there's Alotta Fagina, Ivana Humpalot, Fook Mi and Fook Yu (the Japanese twins), Dixie Normous, Felicity Shagwell ("Shagwell by name, shag very well by reputation."), Robin Swallows (maiden name Spitz)... anyone else?

tropes.name: Regional Bonus
tropes.html: A few countries had a cut with deleted scenes, including Christian Slater's cameo and the death of mooks being mourned (which includes a cameo by Rob Lowe).

tropes.name: Rule of Funny
tropes.html: Honestly, the series has a time-traveling car that travels not by accelerating to 88 miles per hour, but by bouncing really hard on its hydraulic suspension. If you can swallow that but not Vanessa being a Fembot, you need to recite the mantra.

tropes.name: Scenery Censor
tropes.html: Spoofed multiple times.

tropes.name: Screens Are Cameras
tropes.html: Dr. Evil tends to do this a lot. He has typical villain ultimatums with various world leaders through closed circuit televisions, yet there are no cameras that would allow him to see anything.

tropes.name: Shaking the Rump
tropes.html:
• Austin shakes his rear (after stripping down to his underwear) while using his mojo to overwhelm the Fembots.
  • Felicity does this in front of Austin in her first scene, while wearing skin-tight shorts, no less.

tropes.name: Shark Pool
tropes.html:
• Attempted in the first movie, but Number Two couldn't get Dr. Evil sharks due to environmental regulations. They had to make do with (mutant, ill-tempered) sea bass instead.
  • Dr. Evil finally get a shark tank in the third movie.

tropes.name: Shoe Phone
tropes.html: Spoofed with the ridiculous items Austin gets from Basil, including a toothpaste tube containing plastic explosive (Or so Austin thinks).

tropes.name: Shout-Out
tropes.html: Has its own page.

tropes.name: Shown Their Work
tropes.html: Austin's wardrobe was meticulously researched and accurate for the Swinging Sixties period he originally comes from, down to the use of couch and curtain fabric for his suit jackets.<!--* ShowStopper: Parodied.-->

tropes.name: Shut Up, Kirk!
tropes.html:
• After Austin tries to defend his 60s values, Dr. Evil retorts with:
Dr. Evil: Really, there's nothing more pathetic than an aging hipster.
  • In the third movie, when Austin tells Scott that he shouldn't focus so much on earning his father's approval and just love himself, Scott retorts by shushing Austin and spitefully saying that he hates him.

tropes.name: Signature Style
tropes.html: If you've seen the Wayne's World movies, the way Austin Powers gleefully plays with every trope possible and half the time ignores the fourth wall won't be new to you.

tropes.name: The '60s
tropes.html: The setting of the opening of the first and most of the second.

tropes.name: Skirts and Ladders
tropes.html:
• Austin can't help but stare when Vanessa climbs up a ladder ahead of him.
  • Austin can't help but stare when Dr. Evil climbs up a ladder ahead of him (so that he can use a pun with "your nuts" and "you're nuts").

tropes.name: Slow "NO!"
tropes.html:
• Austin cries "No!" in slow motion as he leaps for the button to shut off Project: Vulcan.
  • In the second movie, both Austin and Past Austin invoke this as they leap to catch Austin's mojo.

tropes.name: Something Else Also Rises
tropes.html:
• During the ending of the first movie, Austin reminisces about the moment he and Vanessa met. As he recalls how beautiful and sexy he thought she was, Vanessa gradually blows up a pink, tubular balloon. Austin then asks if Vanessa felt the same way, but Vanessa replies that she actually couldn't stop staring at his teeth. Both Austin and the balloon promptly deflate.
  • In the second movie, Austin is asked to put some lotion on Felicity Shagwell's back, and squeezes the bottle a little too hard...
  • In the third film, Fook Mi and Fook Yu's offer of giving Austin a "top secret massage" is followed by the cap in the beer bottle Austin is holding suddenly flying off, followed by the customary foam.
Austin: Sorry! I swear that never happens...

tropes.name: Spies Are Lecherous
tropes.html: Austin is an extremely promiscuous super-spy who is in his prime during the sexual revolution of the 1960s, and really lives by it. Despite being a homely man with Nerd Glasses and British Teeth, he's extremely popular with the ladies. In his second movie, his "mojo" gets stolen, making him temporarily lose his sexual prowess.

tropes.name: Spiritual Successor
tropes.html: The films follow in the footsteps of the James Bond spoofs of the 1960s, particularly Our Man Flint and Casino Royale (1967).

tropes.name: Spontaneous Choreography
tropes.html: During the opening titles of each movie, Austin engages in this with supposedly random bystanders.

tropes.name: Stating the Simple Solution
tropes.html: Scott Evil keeps goading his father to just shoot Austin.

tropes.name: Suddenly Always Knew That
tropes.html:
• From the second film:
    Austin: Basil! It turns out Vanessa [the female sidekick from the previous film and Austin's wife] was a Fembot!
    Basil: Yes, we knew all along, sadly.
  • Austin and Dr. Evil not only went to Spy academy together, but shared a dorm room. Oh and also, Austin has a father, Nigel Powers, who is England's most famous spy. None of these things are ever mentioned before the third film and then are simply taken as read by all concerned.

tropes.name: Supervillain Lair
tropes.html:
Dr. Evil has them to spare. Brought to its ultimate when Dr. Evil travels back in time and starts getting all the stuff he's used to having as a sixties supervillain:
Young Number Two: Your new lair is up and running.
Dr. Evil: Is it a hollowed-out volcano like I asked?
Young Number Two: Of course.

tropes.name: Surrounded by Idiots
tropes.html:
Dr. Evil feels this way.
Dr. Evil: Why must I be constantly surrounded by frickin' idiots?

tropes.name: Talking Is a Free Action
tropes.html: Generally used, but the second movie is the most blatant about it. Austin time-travels ten minutes back in time to just when Felicity's chamber was being flooded with poison gas... and pauses to have a chat with himself that lasts longer than it originally took the chamber to flood with gas. Time apparently just halts for this, and doesn't start up again until past-Austin shoots some mooks.

tropes.name: Tap on the Head
tropes.html: Austin's judo chops are a straight example.

tropes.name: A-Team Firing
tropes.html: Zigzagged. Austin himself is rather guilty of it, firing in completely random directions and somehow managing to hit almost nothing. Other times, Austin's so accurate that it's a wonder anyone ever gets near him.

tropes.name: Terminator Twosome
tropes.html: Inverted, as Austin and Dr. Evil both travel to the future in the first movie, and played straight, as they travel to the past in the second.

tropes.name: Tie-In Music Video
tropes.html:
The trilogy featured several tie-in music videos with appearances from Mike Myers as the lead character:
  • Madonna's "Beautiful Stranger" (from The Spy Who Shagged Me) involves Austin going to a British club to see her perform, and driving her back to his place afterwards.
  • The music video for Dr. Evil's "Hard Knock Life" (from Goldmember) shows more of the duo's escape from prison.
  • Goldmember also led to a music video of Beyoncé performing as Foxxy Cleopatra for the song "Work It Out".
  • Britney Spears' "Boys" involves Austin trying to dance with the pop singer at an exclusive party.

tropes.name: Time Machine
tropes.html: Dr. Evil has one that just looks like a spinning portal. The British secret service has both a Beetle with a garish paint job in the second film, and a "Pimpmobile" Cadillac Eldorado in the third.

tropes.name: Time Travel
tropes.html: The second and third films use time travel to bring Austin and Dr. Evil back to the '60s (in the second) and '70s (in the third).

tropes.name: Torpedo Tits
tropes.html: The the Fembots have machine guns fitted behind their breasts.

tropes.name: Tuckerization
tropes.html: Given Mike Myers is a huge Toronto Maple Leafs fan, there are two characters named after hockey players, Commander Gilmour (Doug Gilmour - whose first name is also Dr. Evil's real one), and General Borschevsky (Nikolai Borschevsky).

tropes.name: Twisted Echo Cut
tropes.html:
• In The Spy Who Shagged Me, Two Hurricane of Euphemism Overly Long Gags cover a succession of people being distracted by Dr. Evil's rocket, and being cut off just before they can remark that it looks like a giant— Johnson!
  • They do the same gag in Goldmember with the satellite that looks like a pair of big— Bazookas? And so on, though further mixing up the gag by once instead having the euphemism spelled out on-screen instead of being said (and having Ozzy Osbourne scorn the filmmakers as boobs for re-using the joke).

tropes.name: Undignified Death
tropes.html:
Often happens to Dr. Evil's Mooks.
  • Patty O'Brien's attempt to assassinate Austin ends with him being drowned in a toilet.
  • A random henchman is run over by a steamroller - after spending a full minute screaming "No!" instead of just getting out of the way.
  • Felicity shows a guard her bare breasts, causing him to become so overcome with desire that he walks right into a Lava Pit.

tropes.name: Unguided Lab Tour
tropes.html: In International Man of Mystery, Austin and Vanessa disguise as tourists to infiltrate Infocom's headquarters during a tour.

tropes.name: Unwitting Instigator of Doom
tropes.html: Whoever rigged Nigel Powers' car to explode in an attempt to assassinate him— the car's explosion killed Mrs. Powers, and resulted in Dougie being adopted by a Belgian baker, leading to him becoming Dr. Evil and the events of the first three films.

tropes.name: Vanity License Plate
tropes.html:
• Austin's "Shaguar" has "SWINGER" on its plate (with the time machine having "SWINGER2").
  • The convertible driven by Movie Austin in the third film has the licene plate "SHAGUAR"
  • Nigel's mini has the plate "GR8 SHAG".

tropes.name: Video Phone
tropes.html: Austin has one in his car. Very helpful for Basil Exposition to talk to him.

tropes.name: Villain Exclusivity Clause
tropes.html: Dr. Evil appears in every movie as the Big Bad.

tropes.name: "Well Done, Son" Guy
tropes.html:
• Austin just wants his father's approval.
  • Inverted with Scott, who wants nothing to do with Dr. Evil, despite his father's attempts at bonding, then finally wins his dad's respect. Too bad his dad becomes Good.

tropes.name: Where Did We Go Wrong?
tropes.html: Dr. Evil asks where he went wrong out loud in response to Scott Evil not living up to his father's expectations in the first two movies.

tropes.name: Above the Influence
tropes.html: Austin, for all his womanizing, turns down a kiss (and probably more) from Vanessa because she's drunk.

tropes.name: Academy of Evil
tropes.html: The evil medical school Dr. Evil went to.

tropes.name: Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking
tropes.html: While snooping around Alotta Fagina's penthouse, Austin discovers a folder with some of Virtucon's Evil Plans listed inside. In between "Human Organ Trafficking" and "Project Vulcan" is... "Carrot Top Movie".

tropes.name: Artistic License – Geology
tropes.html:
A pretty minor example: Dr. Evil refers to the Earth's core as the "liquid-hot magma core". The Earth's innermost core is a mass of iron and nickel, solidified by the intense pressure around it. Though Dr. Evil might be referring to the outer core, which is liquid.
  • Even if Austin hadn't been able to stop the bomb from going off, it would not have happened anyway since the heat in the outer core, which can reach almost 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit, would have long-since melted the detonation devices into useless clumps of slag and the warhead would have just melted, provided the extreme temperatures didn't cause the drill itself to melt.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Linguistics
tropes.html: Alotta Fajina's last name is pronoucned phonetically as "fah-gy-na" but since she is Italian, it should be pronounced "fah-jee-na".

tropes.name: Artistic License – Physics
tropes.html: The Big Boy rocket begins to glow from re-entry the instant it begins to move downwards. But that glow is caused by compression heating which increases with the density of the atmosphere you're falling through at extreme altitudes it would still have a small effect and outside the atmosphere it does not occur at all.

tropes.name: Author Appeal
tropes.html: Mike Myers said that the reason Divinyls was chosen for the music during the scene with the Fembots was because he was a fan of the song and convinced the studio it was the perfect choice for that moment.

tropes.name: Bathroom Brawl
tropes.html: Austin fights the assassin Patty O'Brian when the latter ambushes him in the restroom. A man outside the stalls overhears Austin grunting "Who does Number Two work for?" and assumes he's just constipated.

tropes.name: Behind the Black
tropes.html: Vanessa and Austin walk down a corridor. Random Task steps out from behind a filing cabinet and smashes their heads together - but they should have seen him as they passed by it.

tropes.name: Big Red Button
tropes.html: Two of them. One aborts the underground drill carrying the nuke, the other activates the base's Self-Destruct Mechanism.

tropes.name: Blind People Wear Sunglasses
tropes.html: When Austin enters a casino bathroom, the bathroom attendant is wearing dark glasses. When Austin sees this, he concludes that the man is blind.

tropes.name: Bowdlerise
tropes.html:
Some TV edits omit any use of "horny". So Austin's infamous "Do I make you horny, baby?" sounds like this instead:
Austin: Do I make you randy? Randy? Do I make you randy, baby?

tropes.name: Brain Bleach
tropes.html: "Margaret Thatcher naked on a cold day! Margaret Thatcher naked on a cold day!"

tropes.name: Bread, Eggs, Milk, Squick
tropes.html: One blue crushed velvet suit, one lacey cravat, one medallion with male symbol, one pair of Italian boots, one vinyl record, "Burt Bacharach Plays His Hits", one Swedish-made penis enlarger pump...

tropes.name: Bring My Brown Pants
tropes.html: When Vanessa asks Austin for his plan to escape the mutated sea bass, Austin replies, "First, I plan to soil myself. Then I'm going to regroup and come up with a new plan. Any thoughts?"

tropes.name: Chekhov's Gun
tropes.html:
• The Swedish-made penis enlarger pump which belongs to no one in particular and certainly not Austin proves to be a surprisingly effective weapon against Random Task.
  • While Austin is being shown gadgets, Vanessa also shows him toothpaste, dental floss and mouthwash- the gag is that none of them are disguised weapons, she just was trying to politely get him to improve his dental hygiene. However, the floss and toothpaste actually do come in handy to escape a death trap later on.

tropes.name: Collapsing Lair
tropes.html: Played with, of course, when Dr. Evil's lair explodes; the actual explosion is shown through grainy old Stock Footage.

tropes.name: Comically Missing the Point
tropes.html:
Vanessa: Well, did you use protection?
Austin: Of course. I had my 9mm automatic.
Vanessa: You know I meant 'did you use a condom'?
Austin: No. Only sailors use condoms, baby.
Vanessa: Not in the '90s, Austin.
Austin: Well they should, those filthy buggers, they go from port to port.

tropes.name: Cosmopolitan Council
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's Council and also, the United Nations have a wide variety of cultures and ethnicities present.

tropes.name: Countrystan
tropes.html: Played for Laughs. Dr. Evil's forces steal a nuclear warhead from a breakaway Russian republic called Kreplachistan. Kreplach are a type of dumpling.

tropes.name: Crazy Memory
tropes.html:
Dr. Evil describes his father as this.
Dr. Evil: He would make outrageous claims, like he invented the question mark.

tropes.name: Cut Lex Luthor a Check
tropes.html: Played for laughs. When Dr. Evil comes out of cryogenic suspension, he immediately draws up outlandish plans to blackmail world leaders for one million dollars. This annoys Number Two to no end, since he has spent the thirty years Dr. Evil was absent building up the front companies they established into a shady but completely law-abiding, legitimate and wildly successful corporation with an annual revenue of nine billion dollars.

tropes.name: Death Trap
tropes.html:
Parodied, of course.
Dr. Evil: No Scott, I have a better idea. I'm going to place him in an easily escapable situation involving an overly elaborate and exotic death... [Beat] ...what?

tropes.name: Deer in the Headlights
tropes.html: Parodied with the guard and the steamroller.

tropes.name: Deliberate Values Dissonance
tropes.html: The movie gets a number of jokes about The '60s and The '90s being different decades with different social mores. Austin ends up declaring that the actual acts of liberal drug use and sex of the sixties wasn't just about liberal drug use and sex for the sake of having those things, it was about freedom, and expressing and enjoying that freedom, a spirit that lives on strong in the nineties.

tropes.name: Did I Just Say That Out Loud?
tropes.html:
Austin's got a problem separating his inner and outer voices. The Human Popsicle process has some drawbacks.
Austin: My God, Vanessa's got a fantastic body. I bet she shags like a minx. How do I tell them that, because of the unfreezing process, I have no Inner Monologue? I hope I didn't say that out loud just now.

tropes.name: Didn't Think This Through
tropes.html: This is what gets Number Two killed in the climax (at least until his resurrection in the next film). Number Two seats himself at Dr. Evil’s conference table, intending to negotiate with Austin. Therein lies Number Two’s mistake: he’s seated himself at a conference table where (as he should know from 30 years of experience) every single seat is rigged to dump its occupant into the fire pit beneath the floor. And Dr. Evil, who he's betraying, is currently being held at gunpoint on the other side of the table and is mere inches from the kill switch.

tropes.name: Disguised in Drag
tropes.html:
One of Dr. Evil's assassins disguises himself as a waitress at the club that Austin and Mrs. Kensington go to. Austin sees right through it.
Mrs. Kensington: Austin, why on Earth did you punch that woman?
Austin: That's not a woman. It's a man, man. [pulls off the hat and wig]

tropes.name: Does This Remind You of Anything?
tropes.html:
Dr. Evil's warhead.
Austin: Does that make you horny?
Vanessa: Not now, Austin!

tropes.name: Early-Installment Weirdness
tropes.html: Despite all of the goofy comedy, the film is more straightforward as a parody of 60's Bond films. It even features some suprisingly-poignant personality growth for Austin himself, who, being confronted with the realities of the world he wakes up in and his fledgling relationship with Vanessa, slowly changes into a more mature version of himself. Nearly all of this is ejected for the sequels, which choose instead to focus on a more Denser and Wackier approach, fourth wall breaking, and LOTS of self-deprecation and toilet humor.

tropes.name: EgoCorp
tropes.html: Dr Evil has a business arrangement with Mr Roboto, a Japanese businessman and owner of Roboto Industries.

tropes.name: Elaborate Underground Base
tropes.html:
Dr. Evil has one.
Dr. Evil: Welcome to my UNDERGROUND LAIR!!

tropes.name: Even Mooks Have Loved Ones
tropes.html: A few scenes (which were cut from the American release, but included in most international ones) are cutaways about the friends and loved ones of guards Austin kills being informed: one with friends at his bachelor party wondering why he's late, and the other his girlfriend and her son (who considers the guard a substitute father figure).

tropes.name: Exposed Embarrassing Purchase
tropes.html:
The Swedish Penis Enlarger Pump, though in this case he'd already bought it and wasn't in a store. His embarrassment isn't helped by the fact that he kept all the purchase information... or that he apparently wrote a book about how much he loves it.
Clerk: [giving Austin back his items] One Swedish-made penis enlarger pump.
Austin: (to Vanessa, embarrassed) That's not mine.
Clerk: One credit card receipt for Swedish-made penis enlarger signed by Austin Powers.
Austin: I'm telling ya, baby, that's not mine!
Clerk: One warranty card for Swedish-made penis enlarger pump, filled out by Austin Powers.
Austin: I don't even know what this is! This sort of thing ain't my bag, baby!
Clerk: One book, Swedish-Made Penis Enlargers and Me (This Sort of Thing Is My Bag, Baby). By Austin Powers.
Austin: (stunned) ...Ah.
Clerk: Just sign the form.

tropes.name: The Faceless
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's face is never seen in the beginning of the film. It is finally seen after he burns Mustafa alive and says, "Let this be a lesson to you all that this organization will not tolerate failure," revealing that the villain of the movie is also played by Mike Myers.

tropes.name: Failed Future Forecast
tropes.html: In-universe Austin, after being frozen in 1967 and unfrozen in 1997, is shocked at the presence of a Russian intelligence officer. When he is told that the Cold War ended, he initially assumes that the Communists won.

tropes.name: Fetal Position Rebirth
tropes.html: Austin Powers adopts this position when he's unfrozen.

tropes.name: Fiendish Fish
tropes.html: Played for Laughs. Dr. Evil asked his henchmen for a Shark Pool with Frickin' Laser Beams attached to their heads, but they had to settle for "ill-tempered mutant seabass". He gets his wish in later movies, however.

tropes.name: Fish out of Temporal Water
tropes.html:
Austin and Dr. Evil have to face the changes arisen from being frozen 30 years. Which includes:
  • Two plots Dr. Evil cooked up in the 60's have already happened in the 90's. He's too late to the punch to damage the ozone layer and his Royal Family sex scandal plot won't work because there already was a Royal Family sex scandal.
  • Austin's swinging lifestyle and velvet suits are no longer in fashion in the 90's and he now comes off as weird instead of hip.
  • Both of them being deeply confused by modern technology and culture.

tropes.name: Flipping the Bird
tropes.html: Mini-Me's favorite method of insult, most often given to Scott and Austin.

tropes.name: Grossout Fakeout
tropes.html: Several variants of this trope were used in the trilogy; most notably Austin's fight in a toilet stall with O'Brien in the first film (the man in the stall next to him thinks Austin is constipated), and the two "silhouette gags" in the latter two movies (a scene with Austin and Felicity in a tent in the second film makes it look like Felicity is preforming a series of Ass Shoves, while in the third film Austin and Mini-Me are behind a privacy screen and make it look like Austin has a Gag Penis).

tropes.name: Gross-Up Close-Up
tropes.html:
One of the scene transitions ends with a close-up of Austin's bad teeth for no reason.
  • The fact that Ms. Kensington had brought it up immediately before the transition isn't a reason?

tropes.name: Hazmat Suit
tropes.html: The radiation suit Dr. Evil wears is a parody of the one worn by the title character in Dr. No.

tropes.name: Hook Hand
tropes.html: Don Luigi, one of the assassins who Dr. Evil executes for failing to kill Austin Powers, has one of these. He uses it to smoke cigars.

tropes.name: Human Popsicle
tropes.html: Austin and Dr. Evil.

tropes.name: Hypocrite
tropes.html: Dr. Evil shows no care for Scott whatsoever when Austin takes him hostage, and tells him to his face that he had the father/son group "liquidated". Yet when Scott tells his father he hates him, Dr. Evil claims that it hurt his feelings.

tropes.name: I Have Your Wife
tropes.html: Though Austin hadn't married Vanessa yet at this point, Alotta Fagina takes Vanessa hostage when Austin is on the verge of bringing Dr. Evil to justice. This gives Dr. Evil a chance to escape, despite the failed insurrection by Number Two and Vanessa knocking Alotta out and escaping with Austin.

tropes.name: Implausible Deniability
tropes.html: Austin's increasingly desperate insistence that "Swedish-Made Penis Enlarger Pump" wasn't his bag, baby, as the evidence continued to mount against him.

tropes.name: Inflation Negation
tropes.html: One meeeeeeeee-llion dollar ransom. Memetic Mutation as well. This was so ubiquitous, even King Hussein of Jordan joked around with it.

tropes.name: Instantly Proven Wrong
tropes.html:
Austin is repeatedly called out for his ownership of a Swedish penis-enlarger pump while he's picking up his belongings after the unfreezing process. This embarrasses him in front of Vanessa Kensington and causes him to resort to Implausible Deniability.
Clerk: One Swedish-made penis enlarger pump...
Austin: That's not mine.
Clerk: One credit card receipt for Swedish-made penis enlarger, signed by... Austin Powers.
Austin: [to Vanessa] I'm telling you, baby, that's not mine.
Clerk: One warranty card for Swedish-made penis enlarger pump, filled out by... Austin Powers.
Austin: I don't even know what this is. This sort of thing ain't my bag, baby.
Clerk: One book: Swedish-made Penis Enlarger Pumps and Me: (This Sort of Thing Is My Bag, Baby), by... Austin Powers.
Austin: Ah.

tropes.name: Intimate Artistry
tropes.html: Austin was flirting with Vanessa from the very instant that he awoke from his cryogenic freezing, but he only seemed to progress from purely-physical attraction to an emotional connection when she briefly posed for photographs for him when they were on a surveillance mission. After saying how beautiful she was he took her out for a night on the town, where she first began to return his affections.

tropes.name: Inventor of the Mundane
tropes.html: During a group therapy session Dr. Evil mentions that his father claimed to have invented the question mark (among many other, equally strange declarations).

tropes.name: Ironic Echo
tropes.html: See Instantly Proven Wrong above.

tropes.name: It's Been Done
tropes.html:
When he's unfrozen, Dr. Evil suggests evil plans that are moot because they've already happened (ruining Prince Charles's marriage, punching a hole in the ozone layer).
Dr. Evil: Right, people, you have to tell me these things, okay? I've been frozen for thirty years, okay? Throw me a frickin' bone here!

tropes.name: Just a Gangster
tropes.html: When Dr. Evil is unfrozen, he insists on bringing his organization back to its old ways despite the fact that it has become much more successful and lucrative as a legitimate business.

tropes.name: Just in Time
tropes.html: Played for laughs. Austin has well over ten seconds to stop Dr. Evil's drill from reaching the Earth's core, but deliberately waits until there's just a second to spare, so that his Big "NO!" will look more dramatic.

tropes.name: Kavorka Man
tropes.html:
Despite his lecherous behavior, yellow, crooked teeth, and general lack of game, woman still seem ridiculously attracted to him. Lampshaded by Mrs. Kensington telling Vanessa more about Austin.
Mrs. Kensington:In the sixties, you could be a sex symbol and still have bad teeth. It didn't matter!

tropes.name: Kirk Summation
tropes.html:
Austin's response to Dr. Evil's "Not So Different" Remark attempt.
Austin: I've got you, Dr. Evil!
Dr. Evil: Well done, Mr. Powers. We're not so different, you and I. It's true, you're British, and I'm Belgian. You have a full head of hair, mine is slightly receding. You're thin, I'm about forty pounds overweight. OK, we are different, I'm not making a very good point. However, isn't it ironic, Mr. Powers, that the very things you stand for: swinging, free love, parties, distrust of authority- are all now, in The '90s, considered to be... evil? Maybe we have more in common than you care to admit.
Austin: No, man, what we swingers were rebelling against were uptight squares like you, whose bag was money and world domination. We were innocent, man. If we'd known the consequences of our sexual liberation, we would have done things differently, but the spirit would have remained the same. It's freedom, man.
Dr. Evil: Your freedom has caused more pain and suffering in the world than any plan I ever dreamed of. Face it, freedom failed.
Austin: No, man, freedom didn't fail. Right now, we've got freedom and responsibility.

tropes.name: Lame Rhyme Dodge
tropes.html:
Dr. Evil: Son, wouldn't you like to see what daddy does for a living?
Scott Evil: Blow me.
Dr. Evil: What?
Scott Evil: Show me.
(The TV edited version works just as well:)
Dr. Evil: Son, wouldn't you like to see what daddy does for a living?
Scott Evil: Bite me.
Dr. Evil: What?
Scott Evil: Might be... fun.

tropes.name: Low-Speed Chase
tropes.html: Austin and Vanessa try to escape pursuing guards in a steamroller that moves so slowly that the guards should be able to easily catch up to them.

tropes.name: Mission Creep
tropes.html: Parodied. The defrosted Dr. Evil returning from The '60s to The '90s tries to launch into an old-fashioned spy supervillain plot only to be reminded that his organization in his absence had to Cut Lex Luthor a Check and branch into legitimate corporate enterprise so as to better serve evil of course.

tropes.name: Mistaken for an Imposter
tropes.html: "That's not your mother, it's a MAN, Baby!... WHY! WON'T this WIG! come OFF!"

tropes.name: Mugged for Disguise
tropes.html: Subverted and parodied. When Austin and Vanessa are infiltrating Virtucon, they notice an extremely heavyset female scientist and a thin, lanky scientist almost seven feet tall go into the restrooms; they follow them, and emerge wearing a pair of perfectly-fitting uniforms. They also do this right in front of the tour guide, who alerts the guards, making the whole charade pointless.

tropes.name: Naked People Are Funny
tropes.html: There's two Overly Long Gags in which Austin and latter Vanessa make full use of Scenery Censor.

tropes.name: Neck Lift
tropes.html: When Random Task attacks Austin Powers near the end, he grabs him by the neck, lifts him up and presses him against a wall.

tropes.name: Newspaper-Thin Disguise
tropes.html: Austin attempts to disguise himself with a magazine... with his own face on the cover.

tropes.name: Next Stall Shenanigans
tropes.html:
Austin's visit to the can is interrupted by an assassin, who he eventually overpowers and drowns in the toilet. While this is going on, the guy in the next stall is keeping a running commentary on what he's hearing.
*Austin puts the assassin head-first into the toilet*
Austin: Who does Number Two work for?!
Other guy: That's right, buddy, you show that turd who's boss!
[the assassin starts noisily drowning]
Other guy: Hey, uh, that sounds pretty nasty. How about a courtesy flush over there?

tropes.name: NO INDOOR VOICE
tropes.html: "I'm finding it hard to control THE VOLUME OF MY VOICE!"

tropes.name: No, Mr. Bond, I Expect You to Dine
tropes.html:
Lampshaded and spoofed.
Scott: What, you're feeding him? Why don't you just kill him?

tropes.name: No-Nonsense Nemesis
tropes.html:
Scott Evil is outraged by his daddy Dr. Evil's dogged insistence on Bond Villain Stupidity by having dinner with his arch-enemy Austin Powers and deciding to place him in an easily escapable Death Trap. Scott offers to just shoot the super-spy and be done with it, but Dr. Evil simply ignores him.
Dr. Evil: Scott... you just don't get it.

tropes.name: Outfit-Rip Sex Check
tropes.html:
• Early in the film Powers grabs a pretty mod girl and declares "it's a man, man!" and pulls her wig off, revealing a male spy.
  • Later in the film, Powers meets Basil Exposition's mother and he thinks it's another male spy in a little old lady disguise, but it turns out this one really is a little old lady.

tropes.name: Overly Long Scream
tropes.html:
Parodied. A Mook lets off a few loud Big "NO!" screams, one after another, as a steamroller is about to crush him. This is despite the fact that he's several yards away from the steamroller, which is going so slowly that the mook could just walk to escape it.
"NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!!! NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!!!!! NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!! NOOOOOOOAAAAAHHHHH-" [steamroller runs him over]

tropes.name: People Jars
tropes.html: There is a cryogenic storage facility with frozen celebrities in pods. Amongst them Vanilla Ice◊.

tropes.name: Planetary Core Manipulation
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's nefarious plot is to use a "big underground drill" to penetrate the Earth's crust and plant a 50 kiloton nuclear warhead deep in the core of the planet. When the bomb detonates, every volcano on Earth will erupt simultaneously.

tropes.name: Player Nudge
tropes.html:
The blackjack dealer at the casino does this twice.
  • The first time, he advises Number Two against hitting on 17. Number Two ignores this, saying, "I like to live dangerously." Unbeknownst to the dealer, Number Two used the X-ray vision from his eyepatch to see that his next card will put him at 21.
  • The second time, Austin wants to stay on 5. The dealer tells Austin to hit, but Austin says, "I also like to live dangerously." The dealer easily beats Austin's 5 with 20.

tropes.name: Pop-Cultural Osmosis Failure
tropes.html:
Patty O'Brian can't understand why people keep laughing when he says Interpol are "after [his] lucky charms".
  • Played for Drama between Austin and Vanessa, with his one night stand with Alotta Fagina threatening to torpedo their relationship. Vanessa is disgusted Austin had unprotected sex with a woman he hardly knows, while Austin, a swinger from the "free love" era, doesn't see anything wrong.

tropes.name: Post-Climax Confrontation
tropes.html: At the end during Austin and Vanessa's honeymoon, Random Task shows up again to kill them... and is defeated with the help of the penis enlargement pump.

tropes.name: Punctuated!  For!  Emphasis!
tropes.html: "DO! YOU! WORK! FOR! NUMBER! TWO!??" (original release version. The current releases use the clip of Austin shouting "Who... does... Number Two... work for?!")

tropes.name: Punny Name
tropes.html: According to the DVD Commentary, the Sphynx cat playing Mr. Bigglesworth was called Ted Nude-Gent.

tropes.name: Put Their Heads Together
tropes.html: As Austin and Vanessa are infiltrating Virtucon, Random Task comes up behind them and cracks their heads together, knocking them out.

tropes.name: Pyrrhic Victory
tropes.html: When Austin catches Dr. Evil attempting to escape after Austin stopped the nuclear warhead, Dr. Evil attempts to impose this on Austin. He argues that free love and anything Austin stood up for in the 1960's is considered "evil", but Austin argues that they aren't and he's come to understand how much the world changed but can be similar motives adapted for the 1990's, saying "It's freedom, baby, Yeah!" Dr. Evil is still smug that even though Austin has caught him, Dr. Evil says "Freedom failed" and Austin would be forced to live with all that, and not in a good way. Luckily for Dr. Evil, Alotta Fagina arrives holding Vanessa hostage. This gives Dr. Evil a chance to escape after a failed intervention by Number Two.

tropes.name: Rank Up
tropes.html: At the end of the movie, Basil informs Vanessa that she's been made a full agent.

tropes.name: Rip Van Tinkle
tropes.html: Austin's epic urination after being awakened from cryo-sleep.

tropes.name: Sealed Evil in a Can
tropes.html: The freezing of Dr. Evil.

tropes.name: Sealed Good in a Can
tropes.html: The freezing of Austin.

tropes.name: Self-Destruct Mechanism
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's underground base in the first film and moon base in the second one has them. Which can causes the bases to, well, self-destruct.

tropes.name: Sexophone
tropes.html: When Austin first encounters the Fembots, saxophone music plays.

tropes.name: Sexy Silhouette
tropes.html: Alotta Fagina undresses behind a semi-transparent wall, causing Austin's libido to go crazy more than usual.

tropes.name: Shoe Slap
tropes.html: Random Task throws his shoe, as a parody of Oddjob's doing the same with his hat.

tropes.name: Shout-Out
tropes.html: The "Really, there's nothing more pathetic than an aging hipster" line is a reference to Lenny Bruce saying "There's nothing sadder than an aging hipster."

tropes.name: Standard Snippet
tropes.html: George S. Clinton's arrangement of "Rule, Britannia!" as Commander Gilmour is summoned to London.

tropes.name: Suddenly Obvious Fakery
tropes.html: Played for laughs. Austin is in a nightclub when he suddenly screams that an attractive woman is a man. When we cut back to "her", she's suddenly and very obviously a burly, unshaven stunt artist in drag, who attacks Austin.

tropes.name: Swirlie
tropes.html: Austin drowns Patty O'Brien in a hotel toilet.

tropes.name: Take That!
tropes.html: "Carrot Top Movie" is among the Evil Corp's evil plans. note  Chairman of the Board would have been in production around the same time as International Man of Mystery, because it was originally planned for a 1997 release.

tropes.name: A Taste of Their Own Medicine
tropes.html: The Fembots were designed to seduce men so they could kill them. Austin uses the power of his mojo to cause them to overload and explode through sheer desire.

tropes.name: Think Unsexy Thoughts
tropes.html: To resist the fembots, Austin pictures the least arousing things he can think of, including: baseball, taking a cold shower, and "Margaret Thatcher naked on a cold day".

tropes.name: Threatening Shark
tropes.html: Dr. Evil requested that Number 2 provide him with a pool of sharks with "frickin' laser beams attached to their heads". (But he has to do with ill-tempered mutant sea bass. The sharks are an endangered species and too much of a hassle.)

tropes.name: Twinkle Smile
tropes.html: At the end while he's in bed with Vanessa Kensington, Austin does this to show he's embraced dental hygiene.

tropes.name: Twister Game Hijinks
tropes.html: When Austin and Vanessa are in a hotel room together, one scene starts with them hidden behind a sofa. Based on what they're saying to each other, they're apparently having sex. As the camera moves forward to show them, it's revealed that they're actually playing a game of Twister.

tropes.name: Two-Person Pool Party
tropes.html: Austin and Alotta Fagina share a hot tub, spoofing a similar scene from A View to a Kill.

tropes.name: Uranus Is Showing
tropes.html: Austin makes this joke at the end of the movie.

tropes.name: Video Call Fail
tropes.html: After giving the world his ransom demands, Dr. Evil can't figure out the remote control and inadvertently changes the live feed to Beavis and Butt-Head briefly before ending the transmission.

tropes.name: Weather-Control Machine
tropes.html: Dr. Evil mentions that in the 1960's, he had a "weather changing machine that was, in essence, a sophisticated heat beam, which we called a laser."

tropes.name: What Are Records?
tropes.html: Inverted, with Austin trying to play a CD on a turntable.

tropes.name: What Measure Is a Mook?
tropes.html: Mocked in the extended version of International Man of Mystery. We see the family of the dead guard that Austin smashes with the steamroller learning of his death; later, "John Smith", the guard who gets decapitated, by the "ill tempered mutated sea bass," is shown to have been a day away from marriage, and was late for his bachelor party, because he was working late. In both cases, the families and friends are fully aware, that the mook is a henchman of Dr. Evil, and act like it's just a normal job.

tropes.name: Why Don't You Just Shoot Him?
tropes.html: Scott asks this almost verbatim: "why don't you just kill him?", and offers to shoot Austin himself. (Dr.Evil instead lowers Austin and Vanessa into a pool of mutated sea bass.)

tropes.name: You Have Failed Me
tropes.html: Dr. Evil punishes his minions by dumping them through a trapdoor to be burned alive. After being thawed, Dr. Evil is angry that Mr. Bigglesworth is now devoid of fur, blaming this on Mustafa. As punishment, Mustafa gets dumped into the furnace below; he survives, but he's "very badly burned". Shortly thereafter, he's shot by another mook whose first shot registers a non-lethal hit, but gets the kill with the second. His botched execution is Played for Laughs.

tropes.name: You Just Told Me
tropes.html: Subverted. Austin tricks Alotta Fagina, into admitting her boss is into "big underground drills," but he knew already, and did this to look suave. Counts as a spoof as well, since he is the one who brought up the drills, so he obviously already knew.

tropes.name: Your Head A-Splode
tropes.html: This happens to one of the Fembots during Austin's striptease.

tropes.name: Zoomed-Out Reframing Gag
tropes.html: Austin scatters a team of guards while driving a steamroller, except one who can't get out of the way and screams "No!!!" as the steamroller bears in on him. Then the camera pans out to show that the steamroller is about thirty yards away, the steamroller is moving at a speed of inches an hour and he has plenty of time to get out of its path. Instead he just stands there screaming "No!" until the steamroller finally flattens him.

tropes.name: Ain't Too Proud to Beg
tropes.html: Austin tearfully pleads "No more!" after Mini Me pummels him on the moon.

tropes.name: Anachronism Stew
tropes.html: Elvis Costello makes an appearance singing for Austin and Felicity, but the scene in question took place in 1969, which meant he would've only been fifteen years old (and looked much older than that). This is played for laughs like everything else. Burt Bacharach and Woody Harrelson also look to be as old as they were in 1999 in 1969.

tropes.name: Anguished Declaration of Love
tropes.html: When Austin fails to save Felicity in the first run of events, he quietly whispers "I love you, Felicity."

tropes.name: Armor-Piercing Question
tropes.html: Upon being asked if he's happy, Fat Bastard breaks down in tears when he admits he's not. Unusually for this series, it's played relatively straight until he lets out a fart.

tropes.name: Artistic Licence
tropes.html:
To British viewers at least, the "newspaper" Austin reads in the space station is clearly a mockup designed by somebody who has never seen the real paper:
  • Although the paper is nicknamed "the London Times", to distinguish it from similarly-named papers such as the New York Times, its official name (the one on the masthead) is "The Times".
  • The masthead design is totally wrong.
  • In particular, the masthead (like the rest of the paper) is in Times New Roman, not the Fraktur typeface used. (Many British papers have moved away from the Fraktur tradition.)

tropes.name: Artistic License – History
tropes.html:
• Historically, the U.S. president in 1969 was, of course, Richard Nixon. The film just ignores this and instead features a generic fictional president.
  • Dr. Evil's demand for 100 billion dollars is treated as absurd by the government because "that amount of money doesn't even exist" in 1969. In reality, that amount of money did exist in 1969. The federal budget for spending alone was nearly double that at $182.8 billion.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Military
tropes.html: Fat Bastard's OIC is wearing a lance sergeant's forage cap rather than one appropriate to his actual rank of colonel.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Music
tropes.html: Felicity Shagwell's theme, "American Woman", wasn't released until 1970.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Physics
tropes.html: When the President wants to launch nuclear missiles at the moon, he is stopped by his military advisor who asks if he's suggesting they blow up the moon. All the nuclear warheads in the world in 1969 wouldn't even be able to do that. Even if every single nuclear weapon created by NATO and the Warsaw Pact during the Cold War were launched at the moon, a total of over 60'000 nuclear warheads, they wouldn't even crack the surface.

tropes.name: Ass Shove
tropes.html: After charming Fat Bastard into bed, Felicity plants a tracking device on him by shoving it up his buttock cleavage. Fat Bastard thinks she's being "frisky".

tropes.name: Bait-and-Switch
tropes.html:
• While in his pad at 1969, Austin stands beside a woman, and suddenly says "Get your hands off my Heinie, baby!" The woman moves her hand into shot, revealing that she's holding a Heineken beer.
  • After Austin finds out that Felicity got close enough to plant a tracking device on Fat Bastard by having sex with him, he asks her how she could do it. Felicity responds that it's her job to do morally ambiguous things. Then, Austin clarifies that he was asking how she could physically do it due to how big Fat Bastard is.

tropes.name: Bait-and-Switch Comment
tropes.html:
Invoked by Felicity.
Felicity: Well, Austin, I think this time you may have finally met your match.
Austin: Oh no, baby. I've beaten Dr. Evil before, and I'll beat him again.
Felicity: (smirks) I was talking about me.

tropes.name: Batman Can Breathe in Space
tropes.html: Mini-Me is ejected out into space unprotected, and survives completely unharmed (though Dr. Evil thinks this warrants a flu shot).

tropes.name: Big Little Man
tropes.html: Mini-Me's introduction. Upon the announcement that Dr. Evil has been cloned, a regular-sized silhouette of him is outside the door. The door open revealing that said clone is tiny.

tropes.name: Bilingual Bonus
tropes.html: "As the French would say, it has a certain... I don't know what." The phrase je ne sais quoi, a popular term borrowed from French to describe some indescribable aspect of something, literally translates to 'I don't know what'.

tropes.name: Blatant Lies
tropes.html: When Basil tells Felicity not to get too close to Austin, she retorts that her interest in this case is "purely professional" - despite the fact that she had just tried to sleep with Austin.

tropes.name: British Royal Guards
tropes.html: Has a montage where Austin and Felicity goad a royal guard into participating in a Motionless Makeover.

tropes.name: Bulletproof Human Shield
tropes.html:
Robin Swallows can protect Austin from machine gun fire and a bazooka rocket.
Austin: Why Won't You Die?!

tropes.name: Call-Back
tropes.html: Scott suggests that Dr. Evil just go back in time and kill Austin "while he's sitting on the crapper", a nod to Paddy O'Brien's assassination attempt on Austin in the first film.

tropes.name: Captain Obvious
tropes.html: Fat Bastard, after cutting one: "Sorry. I farted."

tropes.name: Censored Title
tropes.html: The movie was often advertised in Britain as "The Spy Who...", leaving out the last two words. In Britain, "shag" is a much dirtier word than it is in North America. Averted or inverted (depending on whether the new title is considered more offensive than the original) in Norway, however, where the title translated as The Spy Who Spermed Me.

tropes.name: Cluster F-Bomb
tropes.html: The Jerry Springer scene. All censored, of course.

tropes.name: Convection, Schmonvection
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's hollowed-out volcano lair, in particular the Lava Pit Death Trap that only burns you if you fall in.

tropes.name: Conveniently Empty Roads
tropes.html: Austin and Felicity are chased down the countryside by one of Dr. Evil's assassins. Not only do they not pass a single other car during the chase, but no one drives by after they capture and interrogate the assassin.

tropes.name: *Cough* Snark *Cough*
tropes.html: Scott mocks Dr. Evil saying his laser will turn the moon into what he calls a "death star" by pretending to cough in order to hide him saying "Ripoff!"

tropes.name: Covert Pervert
tropes.html: When Austin's arrival in the past causes a women to faint, a man catches her... and proceeds to gawk at her figure. This same fellow also openly stares at Felicity's chest when she pulls him in for a dance.

tropes.name: Delayed Ripple Effect
tropes.html: While Fat Bastard steals Austin's mojo in 1969, Austin only realizes he's lost it in 1999.

tropes.name: Distaff Counterpart
tropes.html: In many ways, Felicity is the female equivalent to Austin. With Austin in his currently diminished state, meeting someone who is more like him than he is at the moment further afffects his self-confidence (especially when he forces himself to turn down Felicity's offer of sex).

tropes.name: Does This Remind You of Anything?
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's rocket has a long, slender fuselage and two spherical fuel tanks near the thruster.

tropes.name: Establishing Character Music
tropes.html: Felicity makes her presence known to Austin by dancing provocatively to "American Woman" by The Guess Who.

tropes.name: Even Evil Has Standards
tropes.html:
• Played both ways and for levity during The Jerry Springer Show sequence. Even the Neo-Nazi and the Klansman think Dr. Evil's a freak (and the latter calls him out as such). Dr. Evil, for his part, becomes angry at the Klansman’s verbal disparaging of Scott. Their relationship may be strained, but even Dr. Evil’s not going to let anyone talk to his own son that way (and attacks the Klansman in retaliation).
  • Dr. Evil then invokes it again later when Fat Bastard mocks Austin after learning Felicity slept with the Scotsman. As much as Dr. Evil enjoys seeing Austin in any kind of agony, having to also imagine Fat Bastard naked is just too gross.

tropes.name: Eye Scream
tropes.html: Mini-Me jams his thumbs into Austin's eyes during their fight on the moon.

tropes.name: Failed a Spot Check
tropes.html: When the Fembot Vanessa unleashes her "machine gun jubblies", Austin playfully wonders how he could have missed those during their lovemaking. The Fembot coldly responds "Perhaps next time you should try foreplay!"

tropes.name: Fan Disservice
tropes.html: Naked Fat Bastard. Send the Brain Bleach! Dr. Evil even lampshades this in-universe.

tropes.name: Fantastic Plagiarism
tropes.html: While he's in the past, Dr. Evil claims credit for various contemporary pop cultural fads, such as claiming "One of Us" was a song he invented. Of course, Scott starts calling him out when he comes back.

tropes.name: Faux Paw
tropes.html: When Austin first sees Felicity, He licks his hand and grooms himself like a cat, in some kind of enticement ritual. He follows up by pushing his "paws" forward as he makes his way toward Felicity.

tropes.name: Flirting Under Fire
tropes.html: Austin and Felicity have a tender moment... while standing in a laughably pathetic Death Trap.

tropes.name: Forced Dance Partner
tropes.html:
Austin is drawn to the beautiful and flirty Felicity Shagwell. Before he can embrace her, Robin Swallows suddenly pops up inbetween them, pushing Austin across the dance floor and away from Felicity, to Austin's distress.
Austin: (reaches for Felicity) I want! I want!!

tropes.name: Foreshadowing
tropes.html: Immediately after Frau tells Dr. Evil that she's late, Scott comes through the time portal and joins them. In The Stinger, we learn that he's not a test tube baby, but Dr. Evil and Frau's love child.

tropes.name: A Glass in the Hand
tropes.html: Vanessa in the beginning smashes a champagne bottle in her hand.

tropes.name: GPS Evidence
tropes.html: The heroes are able to find the location of Dr. Evil's volcano lair by analyzing Fat Bastard's stool sample, discovering traces of a rare vegetable that only grows on one island in the entire world.

tropes.name: Hand Signals
tropes.html: Felicity Shagwell uses them to tell her agents to interfere with Robin Spitz Swallows.

tropes.name: Hand Wave
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's new volcano lair is stated to have been built after past Number Two received a "memo from the future".

tropes.name: Happy Ending Override
tropes.html: The film opens on Austin and Vanessa's honeymoon, whereupon Vanessa reveals herself as a Fembot and self destructs.

tropes.name: Head-Turning Beauty
tropes.html: Felicity catches Austin's eye from across the room, and quickly gains the attention of a couple of other men on her way over to him.

tropes.name: Held Gaze
tropes.html: In her first scene, Felicity locks eyes with Austin from across the room, and keeps looking at him even as she dances with two other guys.

tropes.name: Heroic Seductress
tropes.html: Felicity charms Fat Bastard into bed with her so she can plant a tracking device on him.

tropes.name: High-Heel–Face Turn
tropes.html: Ivana Humpalot was sent to kill Austin, but she ends up confessing and sleeping with him instead, simply unable to resist him.

tropes.name: Hoist Hero over Head
tropes.html: Mini-Me lifts Austin up easily (in spite of his small stature), spins him around, then throws him across the corridor.

tropes.name: Hypocritical Humor
tropes.html: After Austin escapes two assassination attempts in a row, Dr. Evil voices his disappointment, claiming that he is "the man who will maintain the dignity of this evil organization"... while driving around in a scooter (with Mini-Me repeatedly honking the horn).

tropes.name: I Ate WHAT?!
tropes.html:
Austin drinks Fat Bastard's stool sample, thinking it is coffee.
Austin: This coffee smells like shit.
Basil: It is shit, Austin.
Austin: Oh, good, then it's not just me. [drinks more] It's a bit nutty.

tropes.name: I'm Mr. [Future Pop Culture Reference]
tropes.html: Dr. Evil uses footage from the film Independence Day to frighten the president and others into thinking the White House is being attacked. But tells him that's what's gonna happen. He calls his moon laser the Death Star and the task of assembling it The Alan Parsons Project. Having gone back to 1969, however, only Scott realizes the idiocy.

tropes.name: Implacable Man
tropes.html: Played for laughs with assassin Robin Spitz-Swallows: she survives a knife in the back, a dozen bullets in the back, a shot from a bazooka in the face, and a ridiculously high fall out of a window with Austin landing on top of her. A spot of Lampshade Hanging occurs when Austin cries "Why won't you die?!" A deleted scene shows that he keeps her in the trunk of his car to deflect gunfire.

tropes.name: Improbable Aiming Skills
tropes.html: Towards the end, Austin fires fewer shots from his handgun than the number of henchmen he hits.

tropes.name: Inelegant Blubbering
tropes.html: Austin openly weeps after the first phase of Mini-Me's attack.

tropes.name: Inflation Negation
tropes.html: Inverted. Dr. Evil's 1969 ransom of one hundred billion dollars doesn't even exist yet.

tropes.name: Instant Seduction
tropes.html: Upon imbibing some of the stolen mojo, Dr. Evil immediately manages to charm Frau.

tropes.name: Intangible Theft
tropes.html: Fat Bastard steals Austin Powers' "mojo" (his libido and sexual prowess) for his arch-nemesis Dr. Evil. It's visualized as a red liquid with little male symbols floating in it.

tropes.name: Intimate Lotion Application
tropes.html: Felicity asks Austin to give her a Massage of Love, which first involves rubbing her back with scented oils. Since Austin has recently lost his mojo (the part of him that makes him so confident and skilled with women), he approaches the act with awkwardness and nervousness, and when she shows her bare back to him he ends up squeezing the bottle so hard the oil spills out.

tropes.name: Island Base
tropes.html: One of Doctor Evil's Evil Lairs.

tropes.name: I Surrender, Suckers!
tropes.html: During their fight in Dr. Evil's moon base, Mini-Me goves Austin the Peace sign, indicating he doesn't want to fight anymore. Austin accepts, only for Mini-Me to attack him while his guard is down.

tropes.name: It's Personal
tropes.html: Both Dr. Evil and Austin say this this in reference to how Dr. Evil's stolen Austin's mojo.

tropes.name: It Was with You All Along
tropes.html: Austin despairs after his mojo is destroyed, believing he's "useless" without it. Felicity points out that he actually had it with him all along, as he was still able to save the world from Dr. Evil.

tropes.name: Lame Comeback
tropes.html:
When Fat Bastard suggests that he and Felicity could have "another go", Austin retaliates rather feebly:
Austin: Shut your mouth, you bastard! ...Who is fat.

tropes.name: Lava Is Boiling Kool-Aid
tropes.html: Though Convection, Schmonvection is played straight, this trope is surprisingly averted. Objects (and people) which fall into the lava do not sink to the bottom, and at no point does the lava "flow".

tropes.name: Leno Device
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's return is announced to the world via...him and Scott appearing on The Jerry Springer Show.

tropes.name: Literalist Snarking
tropes.html:
• Vanessa asks Austin if he smokes after sex. Austin's response? "I don't know, baby. I never look!"
  • Another example is from Austin and Felicity's first meeting.
    Austin: Those are skintight. How do you get into those pants, baby?
    Felicity: You can start by buying me a drink.

tropes.name: The Loins Sleep Tonight
tropes.html: Austin, while in the middle of sex with Dr. Evil's spy Ivana Humpalot, suddenly loses his erection in 1999 when his mojo (libido/sex drive/virility) is stolen from his cryogenically frozen body in 1969. He then travels back to the Swingin' Sixties to reclaim his mojo and cure his erectile dysfunction. His desire to get his groove back is only heightened when the sexy spy/hippie Felicity Shagwell comes his way. With both wanting to shag each other, Felicity increases the swinger's desire to cure his impotency and get his mojo back from Dr. Evil so Austin and Felicity can finally do the horizontal tango.

tropes.name: Marshmallow Hell
tropes.html:
While scoping out Dr. Evil's headquarters, Austin is accidentally pulled down into Felicity's breasts.
Austin: Hello, mummy. Mummy, can I have some chocolates? I want some Mars bars! Don't smack my bottom, mummy...

tropes.name: MST3K Mantra
tropes.html: Invoked and lampshaded, when Austin has some issues with temporal causality. Basil Exposition tells him to just relax and try to enjoy it, then looks directly at the camera and tells the audience to do the same.

tropes.name: Naked People Are Funny
tropes.html: The opening credits play over a scene wherein Austin decides to celebrate his newfound singleness by taking a stroll through the hotel in the buff, his naughty parts concealed by various objects.

tropes.name: Neck Lift
tropes.html: Vanessa does this with Austin in the opening scene.

tropes.name: Never the Selves Shall Meet
tropes.html:
Averted, when Austin not only interacts with a ten-minute-younger version of himself, but the two of them apparently wind up engaging in a three-way with Felicity Shagwell.
Austin Powers: Technically it's not cheating, baby!

tropes.name: Never Trust a Trailer
tropes.html: An early trailer made it seem like Robin Swallows had a larger role then she actually did.

tropes.name: No-Holds-Barred Beatdown
tropes.html: Mini-Me inflicts a brutal assault upon Austin, enough that Austin at one point tearfully pleads "No more!"

tropes.name: Not Actually the Ultimate Question
tropes.html:
When Austin asks Felicity how she could sleep with Fat Bastard, she tells him she was only doing her job. Austin replies that he meant that literally, as Fat Bastard is so fat that the idea of him even being able to have sex seems physically impossible.
Austin: The man's so fat, the sheer mechanics of it are mind-boggling.

tropes.name: Not So Above It All
tropes.html:
Jerry Springer gets into a fight with Dr Evil on his show.
Dr. Evil: "He's biting me! He's biting me!"

tropes.name: Offscreen Teleportation
tropes.html: When Dr. Evil and Mini-Me board the rocket to the moon, they are saluted by his minions who then somehow appear on the moon when they get there.

tropes.name: Once More, with Volume!
tropes.html:
Austin is giving a massage to Felicity who, upon being asked how it feels, requests Austin to move his hands further down along her back. Austin misinterprets and asks his same question but with a deeper voice.
Austin: [giving Felicity a massage] How does that feel, baby?
Felicity: Mmm, lower!
Austin: [deeper voice] How does that feel, baby?

tropes.name: O.O.C. Is Serious Business
tropes.html: After Felicity dies, Austin chases Dr. Evil down with the intent to kill him. As in, not with the purpose of arresting a dangerous felon as within his duty as an international man of mystery, but hunting down Dr. Evil for the express purpose of murdering him. Dr. Evil only saves himself by mentioning that Austin could undo Felicity's death by using time travel.

tropes.name: Opening Narration
tropes.html: The late Tony Jay provides the narration for the film's Opening Scroll.

tropes.name: Parody Product Placement
tropes.html: Starbucks features quite heavily in the 90s-set portion of the movie... where it's revealed to be owned by Dr. Evil, courtesy of Number Two's prudent investing. Indeed, his new Supervillain Lair is a (fictional) Starbucks atop the Space Needle. Two even tries to persuade Evil to focus his business more on coffee than evil empires, on the grounds that they'll make a lot more money that way, but Evil is having none of it.

tropes.name: Perspective Reversal
tropes.html: In the first film, Austin upsets Vanessa by sleeping with Alotta as part of the job; in this movie, Felicity upsets Austin by sleeping with Fat Bastard as part of the job.

tropes.name: Pop-Cultural Osmosis Failure
tropes.html: Justified via Dr. Evil's frequent usage of references in his ransom video to the president; they were from media which doesn't even exist yet at the time. Funnily enough, this works in his favor when he "demonstrates" the laser's power by playing footage of the White House blowing up ripped straight from Independence Day, which initially scares everyone in the room into thinking that it was real.

tropes.name: Post-Climax Confrontation
tropes.html: Done with Fat Bastard but he gets defeated with a Groin Attack.

tropes.name: Prove I Am Not Bluffing
tropes.html: Dr. Evil blows up the White House to demonstrate his giant moon based laser... except it was just footage from Independence Day. Dr. Evil defends the real laser effect would be very similar.

tropes.name: Pun
tropes.html: Fat Bastard declares "I have more chins than a Chinese phone book!" when lamenting to Austin and Felicity about his weight.

tropes.name: Riddled and Rattled
tropes.html: Robin's body shakes wildly when Austin's uses her as a shield against a machine gun barrage.

tropes.name: Ridiculous Counter-Request
tropes.html:
When Ivana Humpalot says her name and Austin thinks she's making a request, he replies:
"Yeah, and I want a toilet made out of solid gold. It's just not in the cards now, is it?"

tropes.name: Robotic Reveal
tropes.html: When Austin rips off the Fembot's synthetic skin faceplate in the opening scene.

tropes.name: Rule of Three
tropes.html: Spoofed, where Mustafa, one of Dr. Evil's assassins, always answers a question truthfully the third time it's asked, because he can't stand being asked the same question three times. However, Mustafa will only answer if the same question is asked three consecutive times.

tropes.name: Sadistic Choice
tropes.html: Dr. Evil: Save the world... or save your girlfriend.

tropes.name: Sci-Fi Writers Have No Sense of Scale
tropes.html: When Dr.Evil threatens the President from his moon base, the General asks for permission to launch the U.S's nuclear arsenal to destroy the moon. In reality, the entire U.S nuclear arsenal going off at once would "only" make a crater about 10 km across, which wouldn't even be big enough to see with the naked eye from Earth, let alone destroy the entire thing.

tropes.name: Sequel Reset
tropes.html: "Wait a tick. That means I'm single again! Oh, behave!"

tropes.name: Sexy Surfacing Shot
tropes.html: In a parody of Honey Ryder's iconic scene in Dr. No, Felicity gracefully emerges on the beach in a white bikini...only to be followed by Austin doing the same, to both his and Felicity's confusion.

tropes.name: Shameless Fanservice Girl
tropes.html: Felicity. The majority of her outfits are skimpy and revealing (most likely part of her efforts to seduce Austin), and she has no problem flashing her panties while she and Austin tease a British Royal Guard, or showing her bare chest to an inept guard in order to lure him into her and Austin's cell.

tropes.name: Show Some Leg
tropes.html:
Felicity Shagwell bares her breasts to the one inept guard outside her and Austin's cell.
Felicity: What do you think of these, my man?
Guard: ...Mommy! (absentmindedly walks towards her and falls into the Lava Pit)

tropes.name: Sigil Spam
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's embossed logo can be found on nearly anything — makeup cases, motorized scooters, record turntables, even the doors of Dr. Evil's secret moon rocket.

tropes.name: Silence, You Fool!
tropes.html: "SILENCE! I will not tolerate your insolence!"

tropes.name: Smoking Hot Sex
tropes.html:
• Parodied at the beginning:
    Vanessa: Do you smoke after sex?
    Austin: I don't know, baby, I've never looked.
  • Felicity lights up after having sex with Fat Bastard.
  • Number Two and Number Two—which, technically, isn't cheating.

tropes.name: Snake Versus Mongoose
tropes.html: Dr. Evil says, "Austin Powers... he's the snake to my mongoose, or the mongoose to my snake. Either way it's bad. I don't know animals."

tropes.name: Snap Back
tropes.html:
• Austin had cleaned up his teeth by the end of the first movie, but upon arriving back in 1969, he finds that they have reverted back to their original unhygenic state.
  • While lusting after Felicity, Austin "grooms" himself like a cat, which gets his hair all messed up. But by the time he and Felicity meet face to face, his hair is back to normal.

tropes.name: Something Something Leonard Bernstein
tropes.html: Dr. Evil and Mini Me attempt to perform "What If God Was One Of Us" for their assosciates. Dr Evil can only remember the lyrics to the first two lines and resorts to singing "bloo-bloo-bloo" to fill in the rest.

tropes.name: Space Base
tropes.html: Another one of Dr. Evil's supervillain lairs. He seems to have every variation of this trope covered.

tropes.name: Squirrels in My Pants
tropes.html: During Austin's fight with Mini-Me on the moonbase, Mini-Me rips a hole in the crotch part of Austin's space suit and proceeds to climb inside. Austin initially panics when Mini-Me begins to crawl around inside his suit, but then begins to fidget around and giggle saying that it tickles. He then traps Mini-Me and then proceeds to eject him out the rear end of his suit through a nearby space toilet.

tropes.name: Straight Gay
tropes.html: The Beefeater remains still when Felicity kisses him on one of his cheeks. When Austin does the same to the other cheek, the guard turns toward Austin and cheekily smiles.

tropes.name: Summon Backup Dancers
tropes.html: Felicity does this by pressing a button on Austin's wall. The flat is immediately swarmed by hippies ready for a party.

tropes.name: Surveillance Station Slacker
tropes.html: An operative at a NATO Surveillance facility switches one of the screens he's supposed to be monitoring to The Jerry Springer Show.

tropes.name: Talk Show Appearance
tropes.html: Dr. Evil and Scott go on Jerry Springer as a subject of dysfunctional fathers. Dr. Evil eventually incites a riot by getting into a fight with a Klansman and causes a riot.

tropes.name: Talk to the Hand
tropes.html:
Dr. Evil does this, much to the U.S. President of 1969's confusion, as Dr. Evil's using '90s-era pop culture lines... in 1969.
Dr. Evil: Talk to the hand, 'cause the face don't wanna hear it anymore.
The President: What hand? Talk to your hand?

tropes.name: The Tease
tropes.html: Felicity. As she makes her way over to Austin, she briefly dances with two other guys before pushing them away. She also kisses a British Royal Guard on the cheek in hoping of making him move.

tropes.name: Testes Test
tropes.html: After the Fembot blows up in his face at the beginning of the movie, Austin moves his hands to his crotch, then faces the camera and announces, "Oh, thank God."

tropes.name: Threat Backfire
tropes.html: In a deleted scene, Felicity responds to Austin telling her she's "going the right way for a smacked bottom" with a flirty "I hope so!"

tropes.name: Timey-Wimey Ball
tropes.html:
By virtue of time-travel.
Austin: Wait a tick. Basil, if I travel back to 1969 and I was frozen in 1967, presumably, I could go back and visit my frozen self. But, if I'm still frozen in 1967, how could I have been unthawed in the '90s and traveled back to— [goes cross-eyed in confusion] Oh, no, I've gone cross-eyed.
Basil: I suggest you don't worry about those things and just enjoy yourself. [to the camera] That goes for you all, too.

tropes.name: Trailer Spoof
tropes.html: Had one related to The Phantom Menace.

tropes.name: Trip to the Moon Plot
tropes.html: The movie's third act is about Dr. Evil installing a giant "laser" on the Moon and Austin following him there to stop him.

tropes.name: Unstoppable Rage
tropes.html: After a Klansmen called Scott Evil a "freak", Dr. Evil ends up going ballistic. He ends up fighting even when being restrained by Steve Wilkos and the other members of security, and after seemingly calming down, he then rushes to attack him again (something that never happens on the Jerry Springer show). And then instigates a full-out brawl on the set. Eventually, he seems calmed down... until Jerry Springer tells security to get Dr. Evil out of the premises ("get this jerk out of here"), upon which his rage is reawakened, and he starts fighting with the host, eventually managing to smash a globe in the ensuing stage riot.

tropes.name: Vader Breath
tropes.html: Mocked when Dr. Evil's spacesuit is damaged, giving him a deeper voice and interrupted breathing. Naturally, he takes this moment to tell Austin he is his father. (He isn't really.)

tropes.name: Vocal Dissonance
tropes.html: At one point during the "Just The Two Of Us" musical number, the 2'8" Mini-Me sings a line in a very low baritone voice.

tropes.name: Wave-Motion Gun
tropes.html: The "Death Star" laser. (Ripoff!)

tropes.name: White Flag
tropes.html: Austin waves one when under fire by the Fembot in the opening scene.

tropes.name: Why Won't You Die?
tropes.html: Austin asks this verbatim of Robin Swallows, who shrugs off a lot of lethal attacks.

tropes.name: Writers Cannot Do Math
tropes.html:
• Mini-Me is described as being "one-eighth" Dr. Evil's size. But he's clearly closer to a third of the doctor's size.
  • Fat Bastard is said to weigh a "metric ton". For reference, that would be around 2000 lbs. He may be big, but he doesn't look anywhere near that big.
  • Austin is stated to have traveled back ten minutes in order to save Felicity, despite the fact that those events were closer to five minutes prior.

tropes.name: You Put the "X" in "XY"
tropes.html:
Invked by Austin himself.
Robin Swallows: Tell me, Mr. Powers: Do you swing?
Austin: Are you kidding, baby? I put the "Grr" in "Swinger", baby!"

tropes.name: And the Adventure Continues
tropes.html: Scott becomes the new Dr. Evil, and is apparently slightly more crazy, meaning the Powers family will have many more adventures to come.

tropes.name: Antagonist Title
tropes.html: Being a spoof of the Bond movies, Goldmember is used in place of Goldfinger as the title. Goldmember is indeed the antagonist, just not the only one.

tropes.name: As Long as It Sounds Foreign
tropes.html: Fook Yu, Fook Mi, and Mr. Roboto are not authentic Japanese names.

tropes.name: Big Bad Duumvirate
tropes.html: Dr. Evil teams up with Goldmember against Austin Powers.

tropes.name: Bowdlerize
tropes.html: In-universe, this was the case for Dr. Evil's "It's a Hard Knock Life" music video: Nudity was censored, and Dr. Evil's curse words were edited, radio edit-style.

tropes.name: Bread, Eggs, Milk, Squick
tropes.html:
Austin's "Things to Do Before I Die" checklist:
Become International Man of Mystery.
Save World From Certain Doom.
Find True Love.
Go To Outer Space.
Travel Through Time, Backward and Forward.
Be Cryogenically Frozen.
Catch Dr. Evil in the First Act.
Threesome with Japanese Twins.
Earn Daddy's Respect.

tropes.name: Breaking Old Trends
tropes.html:
Several elements shown in the previous two movies are absent here.
  • There are no Laugh-In-inspired scene transitions.
  • This movie lacks a scene where one of Dr. Evil's Mooks is killed, and Austin launches into a Hurricane of Puns revolving around the circumstances of the death.
  • Austin's Union Jack briefs don't appear.

tropes.name: Breast Attack
tropes.html: Austin subjects Fat Bastard to a double purple nurple during their brief fight.

tropes.name: Cameo Cluster
tropes.html: The opening is full of famous people playing themselves on the set of an In-Universe Austin Powers movie, which is being directed by Steven Spielberg and stars Tom Cruise, Gwyneth Paltrow, Kevin Spacey, and Danny DeVito, with Quincy Jones and Britney Spears (or a fembot thereof) doing the music.

tropes.name: Captain Obvious
tropes.html: Goldmember states the obvious when Dr. Evil starts giving Scott preferential treatment: "It's a power struggle." and "The tiny one can't take the hint."

tropes.name: Casting Gag
tropes.html: Harry Palmer himself, Michael Caine, appears as Nigel Powers.

tropes.name: Compressed Hair
tropes.html: After swimming to Dr. Evil's submarine Foxxy removes her swimcap to reveal short-looking hair. She shakes her head and it explodes, via a cut to Austin, into her usual enormous afro.

tropes.name: Consulting a Convicted Killer
tropes.html: After Austin learns that his father, Nigel, has been kidnapped and the only clue is that the crew of his yacht have had their genitalia painted gold, Austin visits Dr. Evil, who is being held in captivity in a cell much like Hannibal Lecter's, to find out who is responsible. Dr. Evil reveals to Austin that Goldmember is behind the abduction.

tropes.name: Continuity Nod
tropes.html: At the end of the first movie, Basil tells Austin that he will be knighted. Early on in this film, Austin is finally knighted.

tropes.name: Conveyor Belt o' Doom
tropes.html:
Parodies a very similar scene from Goldfinger with Austin's dad strapped to a device that moves him genitals-first towards a container pouring molten gold.
Goldmember: Your fajah is about to have an unfortunate smelting accident!

tropes.name: Daddy Didn't Show
tropes.html: Nigel Powers had a tendency for this, to the point Austin starts singing "Daddy Wasn't There", quoted atop that article.

tropes.name: Daddy Issues
tropes.html:
Austin responds to accusations of having "Daddy Issues" with this:
Austin: "Nothing could be My Father from the truth. For me this is a Dad issue....Dead! Dad! Deadbeat dad! Daddy didn't love me!"

tropes.name: Dark Horse Victory
tropes.html: As shown in a Flashback, Dr. Evil was actually the favorite to win the prestigious "International Man of Mystery" position at the secret agent academy. But despite this, Austin ended up receiving that honor instead.

tropes.name: Dead Partner
tropes.html: Foxxy Cleopatra had a partner who was killed by Goldmember, and is determined to bring the villain to justice for it.

tropes.name: Denser and Wackier
tropes.html: Goldmember relies less on parodies of the spy genre and more on broad humor, celebrity cameos and pop culture references that were trending in 2002.

tropes.name: Did I Just Say That Out Loud?
tropes.html:
Austin's got a problem separating his inner and outer voices. The Mole's facial blemishes prove just irresistible.
Austin: MOLE!

tropes.name: Didn't We Use This Joke Already?
tropes.html:
When they reuse the rocket-joke from the second movie.
Ozzy: These filmmakers are just [bleep] boobs!
Kelly: What do you mean, Dad?
Ozzy: Well, they're usin' the same [bleep] jokes they did in the last Austin Powers movie.

tropes.name: DreamWorks Face
tropes.html: The Dr. Evil giant submarine has one. Of course it's based on Dr. Evil's quirk of doing the same thing.

tropes.name: Dude, Not Funny!
tropes.html: Said In-Universe by Austin in regards to his father writing off Austin's quite legitimate complaints about his parenting skills with a joke.

tropes.name: Dull Surprise
tropes.html: The street-market shopper (Fred Stoller) who appears in the third section of the montage ("Are they nice and firm?") has this reaction to the satellite's coming into view.

tropes.name: Even the Subtitler Is Stumped
tropes.html: When Austin reunites with his father, in order to prevent the two American women who were keeping tabs on them from knowing what they are talking about, they opt to discus the details in English English, and communicate entirely in increasingly more nonsensical Cockney slang. The subtitler eventually gives up.

tropes.name: Everyone Went to School Together
tropes.html: It is revealed that Austin, Dr. Evil, Number Two and Basil all went to the secret agent academy at the same time (with Austin and Dr. Evil even sharing a dormitory).

tropes.name: Evil Diva
tropes.html: Britney Spears in the opening sequence, whom confidently rivals Austin in a dance battle, and reveals herself to be a Fembot assassin.

tropes.name: Expository Hairstyle Change
tropes.html: Not actually plot-driven, but Foxxy Cleopatra's hairstyle changes in virtually every new scene she's in.

tropes.name: Faceship
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's sub is modeled after him.

tropes.name: Fake Film Intro
tropes.html: The film opens with an action scene where the series' main characters have now been suspiciously recast - Austin Powers is portrayed by Tom Cruise, Dr. Evil by Kevin Spacey and Mini Me by Danny DeVito. It then cuts to a sound stage, revealing that the opening is just part of an in-universe Austin Powers movie being directed by Steven Spielberg.

tropes.name: Fake-Out Opening
tropes.html: The movie opens with a scene from a film within the film about Austin's life.

tropes.name: Flanderization
tropes.html:
Especially evident in Austinpussy (the movie-within-a-movie in Goldmember).
John Travolta as Goldmember: Hey, assholes! Do I have time for a last smoke and a pancake or what!?

tropes.name: Flashback Cut
tropes.html:
• There's a brief cut back to Dr. Evil's "Not So Different" Remark from the first movie.
  • Austin has one when Mini-Me flashes the "peace" symbol. He did this only to give him the finger and kick Austin in the face.

tropes.name: Freeze-Frame Bonus
